children.translated_text: I bow to <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, <s>Skanda</s>, and <s>Īśvara</s>,
to <s>Brahmā</s>, Fire, <s>Indra</s> and the others, and to <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
At <s>Naimiṣa</s>, the seers beginning with <s>Śaunaka</s>, who were worshipping <s>Hari</s>,
welcomed <s>Sūta</s> in connection with a pilgrimage to holy places and said:
The seers said:

children.text: sūta tvaṃ pūjito 'smābhiḥ sārātsāraṃ vadasva naḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s>, you have been honored by us; tell us the essence of the essence,
by the mere knowledge of which omniscience arises.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The essence of the essence is indeed the blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the all-pervading maker of creation and the rest.
Knowing him as "I am <s>Brahman</s>," omniscience arises.

children.text: dve brahmaṇī veditavye śabdabrahma paraṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: Two forms of <s>Brahman</s> are to be known: verbal <s>Brahman</s> and that which is supreme.

children.text: dve vidye veditavye hi iti cātharvaṇī śrutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Two knowledges indeed are to be known," so says the Atharvan revelation.

children.text: ahaṃ śukaś ca pailādyā gatvā badarikāśramam
children.translated_text: I, <s>Śuka</s>, and those beginning with <s>Paila</s> went to <s>Badarikāśrama</s>.
Having bowed to <s>Vyāsa</s>, we questioned him, and he then told us the essence.
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:

children.text: śukādyaiḥ śṛṇu sūta tvaṃ vaśiṣṭho māṃ yathābravīt
children.translated_text: With <s>Śuka</s> and the others, listen, <s>Sūta</s>, to what <s>Vaśiṣṭha</s> told me,

children.text: brahmasāraṃ hi pṛcchantaṃ munibhiś ca parātparam ||
children.translated_text: when I, together with the sages, asked about the essence of <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme beyond the supreme."
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> said:
I shall explain the twofold nature of <s>Brahman</s>; listen, <s>Vyāsa</s>, follower of all tradition,
as Fire once taught me in the company of sages and deities.
This supreme <s>Āgneya</s> Purāṇa is the imperishable supreme knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>;
the other <s>Brahman</s> is the <s>Ṛgveda</s> and the rest, bringing happiness to all the gods.
The Purāṇa spoken by <s>Agni</s>, called <s>Āgneya</s>, is equal to <s>Brahman</s>;
it is divine and grants enjoyment and liberation to people who recite and hear it.
He questioned the god, <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the form of Time-Fire, the light, the supreme <s>Brahman</s> beyond the highest,
who was honored by the sages with knowledge and rites.
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> said:
Tell of <s>Brahman</s>, the Lord, the boat for crossing the ocean of saṃsāra,
the essence of knowledge, by knowing which a man becomes omniscient."
<s>Agni</s> said:
I am <s>Viṣṇu</s>, Time-Fire, and <s>Rudra</s>; I shall tell you the essence of knowledge,

children.text: vidyāsāraṃ purāṇaṃ yat sarvaṃ sarvasya kāraṇaṃ ||
children.translated_text: the Purāṇa that is the essence of knowledge, everything and the cause of everything:
creation, secondary creation, dynasties, and manvantaras,
as well as accounts of dynasties and so on, assuming forms such as <s>Matsya</s> and <s>Kūrma</s>.

children.text: dve vidye bhagavān viṣṇuḥ parā caivāparā ca ha
children.translated_text: The blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the two knowledges, the higher and also the lower.
The Vedas called <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, and <s>Atharvan</s>, and the six Vedāṅgas, O twice-born one,

children.text: śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ jyotiṣāṃ gatiḥ
children.translated_text: phonetics, ritual procedure, grammar, etymology, the course of astronomy,
meter, lexicography, Mīmāṃsā, Dharmaśāstra, and Purāṇa,
logic, medicine, music, Dhanurveda, and Arthaśāstra:
this is the lower knowledge; the higher knowledge is that by which <s>Brahman</s> is reached.
That which is invisible, ungraspable, without family or lineage, and fixed,

children.text: viṣṇunoktaṃ yathā mahyaṃ devebhyo brahmaṇā purā
children.translated_text: as it was told to me by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and formerly by <s>Brahmā</s> to the gods,
so I shall tell it to you, the cause that assumes forms such as <s>Matsya</s>."

children.text: ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye praśno nāma prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the first great Purāṇa, the <s>Āgneya</s>, the first chapter, named "The Question."
<s>Vaśiṣṭha</s> said:
Tell of <s>Viṣṇu</s> in forms such as <s>Matsya</s>, the cause of creation and the rest,

children.text: purāṇaṃ brahma cāgneyaṃ yathā viṣṇoḥ purā śrutam ||
children.translated_text: and of the Purāṇa and <s>Brahman</s> that are <s>Āgneya</s>, as it was formerly heard from <s>Viṣṇu</s>."
<s>Agni</s> said:

children.text: matsyāvatāraṃ vakṣye 'haṃ vasiṣṭha śṛṇu vai hareḥ
children.translated_text: I shall tell of <s>Hari</s>'s Matsya avatāra, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>; listen indeed.
The activity of an avatāra is for the destruction of the wicked and the protection of the good.
At the end of a past kalpa there was the occasional dissolution belonging to <s>Brahmā</s>.
There the worlds beginning with earth were flooded by the ocean, O sage.
<s>Vaivasvata Manu</s> performed austerity for enjoyment and liberation,
and one day, while he was making a water offering in the <s>Kṛtamālā</s>,
a single small fish fell into the water in his joined palms.

children.text: kṣeptukāmaṃ jale prāha na māṃ kṣipa narottama ||
children.translated_text: When he wished to throw it into the water, it said, 'Do not throw me, best of men.

children.text: grāhādibhyo bhayaṃ me 'dya tac chrutvā kalaśe 'kṣipat
children.translated_text: Today I fear crocodiles and the like.' Hearing this, he placed it in a jar.

children.text: sa tu vṛddhaḥ punarmatsyaḥ prāha taṃ dehi me bṛhat ||
children.translated_text: But that fish grew, and again said to him, 'Give me a large
place.' Hearing that speech, the king then placed it in a water pot.

children.text: tatra vṛddho 'bravīdbhūpaṃ pṛthu dehi padaṃ mano ||
children.translated_text: When it had grown there, it said to the king, 'Give me a broad place, <s>Manu</s>.'
Cast again into a lake, it grew to the same size as that.

children.text: ūce dehi bṛhat sthānaṃ prākṣipaccāmbudhau tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: It said, 'Give me a larger place,' and he then threw it into the ocean.
In a mere moment it became one hundred thousand yojanas wide.

children.text: matsyaṃ tamadbhutaṃ dṛṣṭvā vismitaḥ prābravīn manuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing that marvelous fish, <s>Manu</s>, astonished, said:

children.text: ko bhavān nanu vai viṣṇur nārāyaṇa namo 'stu te
children.translated_text: 'Who are you? Surely you are <s>Viṣṇu</s>. O <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, homage to you.

children.text: māyayā mohayasi māṃ kimarthaṃ tvaṃ janārdana ||
children.translated_text: Why do you bewilder me with your māyā, <s>Janārdana</s>?'
Addressed by <s>Manu</s>, the Fish spoke to <s>Manu</s>, who was devoted to protection:
'I have descended for the welfare of this world and for the destruction of the wicked.

children.text: saptame divase tv abdhiḥ plāvayiṣyati vai jagat
children.translated_text: On the seventh day the ocean will indeed flood the world.

children.text: upasthitāyāṃ nāvi tvaṃ bījādīni vidhāya ca ||
children.translated_text: When the boat has arrived, place seeds and the rest in it.
Surrounded by the seven seers, you will pass through <s>Brahmā</s>'s night.
With the great serpent, tie the boat to my horn when I have appeared.'
Having said this, the Fish disappeared. <s>Manu</s>, waiting for the time,
stood by the swelling ocean and then climbed aboard the boat.
The Fish, golden, bearing a single horn, and a niyuta of yojanas long, appeared.

children.text: nāvam babandha tacchṛṅge matsyākhyaṃ ca purāṇakam ||
children.translated_text: He tied the boat to that horn, and the Purāṇa called Matsya

children.text: śuśrāva matsyātpāpaghnaṃ saṃstuvan stutibhiś ca taṃ
children.translated_text: he heard from the Fish, destroyer of sin, while praising him with hymns.
And <s>Keśava</s> slew the demon <s>Hayagrīva</s>,
the thief of the <s>Brahmā</s>-Veda, and protected the Vedas, <s>Matsya</s> and the others.
Then, when the Varāha kalpa had arrived, <s>Hari</s> took the form of <s>Kūrma</s>."

children.text: ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye matsyāvatāro nāma dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the Āgneya Ādimahāpurāṇa, the second chapter, named the Fish Incarnation, is concluded.
<s>Agni</s> said:
I shall also tell of the Tortoise Incarnation, which, when heard, destroys sin.

children.text: purā devāsure yuddhe daityair devāḥ parājitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Long ago, in the war between the gods and the demons, the gods were defeated by the daityas.
And then, through the curse of <s>Durvāsas</s>, they became bereft of splendor.

children.text: stutvā kṣīrābdhigaṃ viṣṇum ūcuḥ pālaya cāsurāt ||
children.translated_text: Having praised <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who dwelt in the milk-ocean, they said, 'Protect us from the asuras.'

children.text: brahmādikān hariḥ prāha sandhiṃ kurvantu cāsuraiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> said to <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, 'Let them make peace with the asuras.
For the asuras should be joined with you for the churning of the milk-ocean, for the sake of nectar and prosperity.
Even enemies should be allied with when the importance of the purpose is great.
I shall make you sharers in the nectar, not the dānavas.'

children.text: manthānaṃ mandaraṃ kṛtvā netraṃ kṛtvā tu vāsukim
children.translated_text: Making <s>Mandara</s> the churning-stick and making <s>Vāsuki</s> the cord,
churn the milk-ocean with my help, without weariness.
Having made the agreement spoken by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, they came with the daityas to the milk-ocean.

children.text: tato mathitumārabdhāḥ yataḥ pucchaṃ tataḥ surāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then they began to churn; where the tail was, there stood the gods.
The gods, scorched by the breaths of the serpent's hoods, were refreshed by <s>Hari</s>.
As the ocean was being churned, that mountain, having no support, sank into the waters.

children.text: kūrmarūpaṃ samāsthāya dadhre viṣṇuś ca mandaram
children.translated_text: Then <s>Viṣṇu</s>, assuming the form of a tortoise, supported <s>Mandara</s>.
And from the milk-ocean as it was churned there arose the poison <s>Hālāhala</s>.
It was held in his throat by <s>Hara</s>; therefore he became <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>, the Blue-throated One.
Then the goddess <s>Vāruṇī</s> arose, and also the <s>Pārijāta</s> and the <s>Kaustubha</s> jewel.
There were cows and divine apsarases; the goddess <s>Lakṣmī</s> went to <s>Hari</s>.
All the gods, seeing her and praising her, became endowed with splendor.
Then <s>Dhanvantari</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the promulgator of <s>Āyurveda</s>,
arose bearing a vessel filled with nectar.

children.text: amṛtaṃ tatkarād daityāḥ surebhyo 'rdhaṃ pradāya ca
children.translated_text: After giving half of that nectar from his hand to the gods, the daityas
took it and went away; then <s>Viṣṇu</s>, source of birth and the rest, assumed a female form.
Seeing her, beautiful in form, the daityas, bewildered, said:
'Become our wife; take the nectar and make us drink it, fair-faced one.'
Saying 'So be it,' <s>Hari</s> took it from them and made the gods drink it.
<s>Rāhu</s>, taking the form of the moon, was drinking, but he was pointed out by the sun and moon.
By <s>Hari</s>'s discus his head was severed apart; that <s>Rāhu</s>,
having been brought to immortality through compassion, spoke to boon-giving <s>Hari</s>:
'When I, <s>Rāhu</s>, am intoxicated, the moon and sun will undergo eclipse by me, the graha.

children.text: tasmin kale ca yaddānaṃ dāsyante syāt tadakṣayaṃ ||
children.translated_text: And whatever gift people give at that time shall be imperishable.'

children.text: tathetyāhātha taṃ viṣṇus tataḥ sarvaiḥ sahāmaraiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> said, 'So be it.' Then, together with all the immortals,
after abandoning the female form, <s>Hari</s> was told by <s>Hara</s>, 'Show it.'
The blessed <s>Hari</s> showed that female form to <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: māyayā mohitaḥ śambhuḥ gaurīṃ tyaktvā striyaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śambhu</s>, deluded by māyā, abandoned <s>Gaurī</s> and went after the woman.
He became naked and like a madman, and he seized the woman's hair.

children.text: agādvimucya keśān strī anvadhāvacca tāṃ gatām ||
children.translated_text: The woman went off after freeing her hair, and he ran after her as she went.

children.text: skhalitaṃ tasya vīryaṃ kau yatra yatra harasya hi
children.translated_text: Wherever <s>Hara</s>'s semen fell upon the earth,

children.text: tatra tatrābhavat kṣetraṃ liṅgānāṃ kanakasya ca ||
children.translated_text: there, in each place, arose a sacred field of liṅgas and of gold.
Knowing, 'This is māyā,' <s>Hara</s> became established in his own nature.

children.text: śivamāha harī rudra jitā māyā tvayā hi me ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> said to <s>Śiva</s>, 'O <s>Rudra</s>, my māyā has indeed been conquered by you.

children.text: na jetum enāṃ śakto me tvadṛte 'nyaḥ pumān bhuvi
children.translated_text: No other man on earth, apart from you, is able to conquer it.'
Then the daityas, not obtaining the nectar, were struck down by the gods in battle.

children.text: tridivasthāḥ surāścāsan yaḥ paṭhet tridivaṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: The gods dwelt in heaven; whoever recites this will go to heaven.

children.text: ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye kūrmāvatāro nāma tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the Āgneya Ādimahāpurāṇa, the third chapter, named the Tortoise Incarnation, is concluded.
<s>Agni</s> said:
I shall tell of the Boar Incarnation, which destroys sin.
<s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, lord of the asuras, existed, and after conquering the gods he stayed in heaven.

children.text: devair gatvā stuto viṣṇur yajñarūpo varāhakaḥ
children.translated_text: When the gods went and praised <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he, as the sacrificial Boar,

children.text: abhūt taṃ dānavaṃ hatvā daityaiḥ sākaṃ ca kaṇṭakam ||
children.translated_text: came into being and killed that dānava, that thorn along with the daityas.
Having protected <s>Dharma</s>, the gods, and the rest, <s>Hari</s> then disappeared.
And <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> was the brother of <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>.
He conquered the gods' shares in sacrifice and took control over all the gods' offices.

children.text: nārasiṃhavapuḥ kṛtvā taṃ jaghāna suraiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: Assuming the body of <s>Narasiṃha</s>, he killed him together with the gods.

children.text: svapadasthān surāṃś cakre nārasiṃhaḥ suraiḥ stutaḥ
children.translated_text: Praised by the gods, <s>Narasiṃha</s> restored the gods to their own stations.
Long ago, in a war between gods and asuras, the gods were defeated by <s>Bali</s> and others.

children.text: jitāḥ svargātparibhraṣṭā hariṃ vai śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ
children.translated_text: Cast down from heaven, they went to <s>Hari</s> for refuge.
Having given fearlessness to the gods, he was praised by <s>Aditi</s> and <s>Kaśyapa</s>.

children.text: stuto 'sau vāmano bhūtvā hy adityāṃ sa kratuṃ yayau
children.translated_text: He became <s>Vāmana</s> in <s>Aditi</s> and went to that sacrifice.
At the royal gate of <s>Bali</s>, who was performing a splendid sacrifice, he recited the Veda.

children.text: devān paṭhantaṃ taṃ śrutvā vāmanaṃ varado 'bravīt
children.translated_text: Hearing that <s>Vāmana</s> reciting for the gods, the boon-giver said:

children.text: nivārito 'pi śukreṇa balir brūhi yad icchasi ||
children.translated_text: Though restrained by <s>Śukra</s>, <s>Bali</s> said, 'Say what you desire.
I shall give that to you.' <s>Vāmana</s> said to <s>Bali</s>:

children.text: padatrayaṃ hi gurvarthaṃ dehi dāsye tamabravīt ||
children.translated_text: 'Give me three steps of ground, for my teacher's sake.' He replied, 'I shall give it.'
When the water had fallen into his hand, <s>Vāmana</s> became no longer a dwarf.

children.text: bhūrlokaṃ sa bhuvarlokaṃ svarlokaṃ ca padatrayaṃ ||
children.translated_text: With three steps he encompassed the earth-world, the mid-world, and the heaven-world.

children.text: cakre baliṃ ca sūtalaṃ tacchakrāya dadau hariḥ
children.translated_text: He sent <s>Bali</s> to <s>Sūtala</s>, and <s>Hari</s> gave that realm to <s>Śakra</s>.

children.text: śakro devair hariṃ stutvā bhuvaneśaḥ sukhī tvabhūt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the worlds, praised <s>Hari</s> together with the gods and became happy.
I shall tell of the incarnation of <s>Paraśurāma</s>; listen, O twice-born one.
Considering the kṣatriyas to be arrogant, he, for the removal of the earth's burden,
descended as <s>Hari</s> for peace, protecting the gods, brahmins, and others.
As the Bhārgava, born from <s>Jamadagni</s> in <s>Reṇukā</s>, he was skilled in weapons.
By the grace of <s>Dattātreya</s>, king <s>Kārttavīrya</s> possessed
a thousand arms; he was lord of the whole earth, and he went hunting.
Exhausted in the forest, he was invited by the sage <s>Jamadagni</s>;
through the power of the wish-giving cow, the king was fed together with his army.

children.text: aprārthayat kāmadhenuṃ yadā sa na dadau tadā
children.translated_text: When he asked for the wish-giving cow and the sage did not give it,
he carried it off. Then <s>Rāma</s> cut off his head and struck him down.
In battle the king was felled by the axe, and the cow returned to her own hermitage.
But by the sons of <s>Kārttavīrya</s>, <s>Jamadagni</s> was slain

children.text: rāme vanaṃ gate vairād atha rāmaḥ samāgataḥ
children.translated_text: when <s>Rāma</s> had gone to the forest. Then <s>Rāma</s> came back,
and seeing his father killed, he was enraged by the destruction of his father.
The mighty one made the earth devoid of kṣatriyas twenty-one times.

children.text: kurukṣetre pañca kuṇḍān kṛtvā saṃtarpya vai pitṝn ||
children.translated_text: At <s>Kurukṣetra</s> he made five pools and duly satisfied the ancestors.

children.text: kāśyapāya mahīṃ dattvā mahendre parvate sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Having given the earth to <s>Kāśyapa</s>, he remained on Mount <s>Mahendra</s>.

children.text: kūrmasya ca varāhasya nṛsiṃhasya ca vāmanaṃ
children.translated_text: After hearing of the incarnations of the Tortoise, the Boar, the Man-lion, the Dwarf,

children.text: avatāraṃ ca rāmasya śrutvā yāti divaṃ naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Rāma</s>, a man goes to heaven.

children.text: ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye varāhanṛsiṃhādyavatāro nāma caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the primordial great Purāṇa, the Āgneya, the fourth chapter, called 'The Incarnation as the Boar, the Man-lion, and the Others.'
<s>Agni</s> said:
I shall tell the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>, as it was formerly spoken by <s>Nārada</s>
to <s>Vālmīki</s>, just as it was recited, granting enjoyment and liberation.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
From the lotus of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s navel came <s>Brahmā</s>; <s>Marīci</s> was the son of <s>Brahmā</s>.
From <s>Marīci</s> came <s>Kaśyapa</s>; from him came the Sun, and <s>Vaivasvata Manu</s>.
Then from him came <s>Ikṣvāku</s>; in his lineage was <s>Kakutstha</s>.
From <s>Kakutstha</s> came <s>Raghu</s>; from him <s>Aja</s>, and then <s>Daśaratha</s>.
For the purpose of killing <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and the others, <s>Hari</s> himself became fourfold.
As <s>Rāma</s> he was born from king <s>Daśaratha</s> in <s>Kauśalyā</s>.

children.text: kaikeyyāṃ bharataḥ putraḥ sumitrāyāṃ ca lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: In <s>Kaikeyī</s> was born the son <s>Bharata</s>; in <s>Sumitrā</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>
and <s>Śatrughna</s>, from the sacrificial rice given to those women by <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s>.
After they had eaten what was produced by the sacrifice, <s>Rāma</s> and the others were equally dear to their father.
Asked by <s>Viśvāmitra</s> to destroy the obstruction to his sacrifice, the king
sent <s>Rāma</s> with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and the sage.
<s>Rāma</s> went, learned missiles and weapons, and killed <s>Tāḍakā</s>.
With the Mānava missile he bewildered <s>Mārīca</s> and drove him far away.
The strong one killed <s>Subāhu</s>, the destroyer of the sacrifice, together with his forces.
Dwelling at <s>Siddhāśrama</s> with <s>Viśvāmitra</s> and the others,

children.text: gataḥ kratuṃ maithilasya draṣṭuṃ cāpaṃ sahānujaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he went with his younger brother to see the sacrifice of the king of <s>Mithilā</s> and the bow.
On account of <s>Śatānanda</s>, the power of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>

children.text: rāmāya kathito rājñā samuniḥ pūjitaḥ kratau ||
children.translated_text: was told to <s>Rāma</s> by the king, and the sage was honored at the sacrifice.
He strung the bow and broke it in sport.

children.text: vīryaśuklāṃ ca janakaḥ sītāṃ kanyāṃ tvayonijām ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Janaka</s> gave <s>Sītā</s>, the maiden not born from a womb, whose bride-price was heroism,

children.text: dadau rāmāya rāmo 'pi pitrādau hi samāgate
children.translated_text: to <s>Rāma</s>; and <s>Rāma</s>, when his father and the others had arrived,

children.text: upayeme jānakīṃ tām ūrmilāṃ lakṣmaṇas tathā ||
children.translated_text: married that <s>Jānakī</s>, while <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> likewise married <s>Ūrmilā</s>.
<s>Śrutakīrti</s> and <s>Māṇḍavī</s>, the two daughters of <s>Kuśadhvaja</s>,
the younger brother of <s>Janaka</s>, were married by both <s>Śatrughna</s> and <s>Bharata</s>.
Those two maidens were married, and they were greatly honored by <s>Janaka</s>.
<s>Rāma</s> went, together with <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and the others, after defeating the descendant of <s>Jamadagni</s>;
and <s>Bharata</s>, together with <s>Śatrughna</s>, went to <s>Ayodhyā</s> from <s>Yudhājit</s>.

children.text: ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye rāmāyaṇe bālakāṇḍavarṇanaṃ nāma pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the primordial great Purāṇa, the Āgneya, the fifth chapter in the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>, called 'The Description of the Bālakāṇḍa.'
<s>Nārada</s> said:
Then, when <s>Bharata</s> had gone, <s>Rāma</s> honored his father and the others.

children.text: rājā daśaratho rāmam uvāca śṛṇu rāghava ||
children.translated_text: King <s>Daśaratha</s> said to <s>Rāma</s>, 'Listen, <s>Rāghava</s>.
Because of their affection for your virtues, the subjects have consecrated you in their minds for the kingdom.

children.text: manasāhaṃ prabhāte te yauvarājyaṃ dadāmi ha ||
children.translated_text: At dawn I shall grant you the office of heir apparent.

children.text: rātrau tvaṃ sītayā sārdhaṃ saṃyataḥ suvrato bhava
children.translated_text: Tonight, together with <s>Sītā</s>, be restrained and firm in good vows.'
And the king's eight ministers, along with <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, spoke likewise:
<s>Sṛṣṭi</s>, <s>Jayanta</s>, <s>Vijaya</s>, <s>Siddhārtha</s>, <s>Rāṣṭravardhana</s>,
<s>Aśoka</s>, <s>Dharmapāla</s>, and <s>Sumantra</s>, together with <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.
Having heard the words of his father and the others, that <s>Rāghava</s> said, 'So be it,'

children.text: sthito devārcanaṃ kṛtvā kauśalyāyai nivedya tat ||
children.translated_text: and remained there after worshiping the gods and reporting it to <s>Kauśalyā</s>.
The king spoke to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and the others about <s>Rāma</s>'s royal consecration:

children.text: sambhārān saṃbhavantu sma ity uktvā kaikeyīṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Let the materials be assembled.' Having said this, he went to <s>Kaikeyī</s>.
Seeing <s>Ayodhyā</s> decorated and knowing that <s>Rāma</s>'s consecration
was about to take place, <s>Mantharā</s>, her companion, told <s>Kaikeyī</s>.
Because she had once been dragged by <s>Rāma</s>, who had seized her feet, for an offense,

children.text: tena vaireṇa sā rāmavanavāsaṃ ca kāṅkṣati ||
children.translated_text: out of that hostility she desired <s>Rāma</s>'s exile to the forest.
'<s>Kaikeyī</s>, get up! <s>Rāma</s>'s royal consecration

children.text: maraṇaṃ tava putrasya mama te nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will be the death of your son and of me; I have no doubt of this.

children.text: kubjayoktaṃ ca tac chrutvā ekamābharaṇaṃ dadau
children.translated_text: Hearing what the hunchback said, she gave her a single ornament

children.text: uvāca me yathā rāmas tathā me bharataḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and said, 'As <s>Rāma</s> is to me, so is my son <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: upāyaṃ tu na paśyāmi bharato yena rājyabhāk
children.translated_text: But I see no means by which <s>Bharata</s> might obtain the kingdom.'
Then angry <s>Mantharā</s>, throwing away the necklace, said to <s>Kaikeyī</s>:

children.text: bāliśe rakṣa bharatam ātmānaṃ māṃ ca rāghavāt
children.translated_text: 'Foolish woman, protect <s>Bharata</s>, yourself, and me from <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: bhavitā rāghavo rājā rāghavasya tataḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāghava</s> will become king, and after him the son of <s>Rāghava</s>.
The royal lineage, O <s>Kaikeyī</s>, will pass away from <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: devāsure purā yuddhe śambareṇa hatāḥ surāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the former war between the gods and Asuras, the gods were struck down by <s>Śambara</s>.

children.text: rātrau bhartā gatastatra rakṣito vidyayā tvayā
children.translated_text: At night your husband went there, and you protected him with your knowledge.

children.text: varadvayaṃ tadā prādād yācedānīṃ nṛpaṃ ca tat ||
children.translated_text: At that time he granted two boons; ask the king for those now.'

children.text: rāmasya ca vane vāsaṃ nava varṣāṇi pañca ca
children.translated_text: And <s>Rāma</s>'s dwelling in the forest would be for nine years and five more,
and the status of heir-apparent he would now give to <s>Bharata</s>.
Incited by the hunchbacked woman, she saw advantage in misfortune,
and said, 'Will he really carry out this good means of mine?'
Then she entered the anger-chamber and fell fainting on the ground.
After honoring the brahmins and others, king <s>Daśaratha</s> then
saw <s>Kaikeyī</s> angry and said, 'Why are you like this?

children.text: rogārtā kiṃ bhayodvignā kimicchasi karomi tat ||
children.translated_text: Are you afflicted by illness, or disturbed by fear? What do you desire? I shall do it.

children.text: yena rāmeṇa hi vinā na jīvāmi muhūrtakam
children.translated_text: By that <s>Rāma</s> without whom I do not live even for a moment,

children.text: śapāmi tena kuryāṃ vai vāñchitaṃ tava sundari ||
children.translated_text: I swear: I will surely do what you desire, O beautiful one.'

children.text: satyaṃ brūhīti sovāca nṛpaṃ mahyaṃ dadāsi cet
children.translated_text: She said to the king, 'If you speak truth and grant it to me,

children.text: varadvayaṃ pūrvadattaṃ satyāt tvaṃ dehi me nṛpa ||
children.translated_text: then give me, O king, the two boons formerly given, in accordance with truth.
Let <s>Rāma</s>, restrained, dwell in the forest for fourteen years,
and with these preparations let <s>Bharata</s> be consecrated here this very day.

children.text: viṣaṃ pītvā mariṣyāmi dāsyasi tvaṃ na cennṛpa
children.translated_text: I shall drink poison and die if you do not grant this, O king.'

children.text: tac chrutvā mūrchito bhūmau vajrāhata ivāpatat ||
children.translated_text: Hearing that, he fainted and fell on the ground like one struck by a thunderbolt.
After a moment he regained consciousness and said this to <s>Kaikeyī</s>:

children.text: kiṃ kṛtaṃ tava rāmeṇa mayā vā pāpaniścaye ||
children.translated_text: 'What has <s>Rāma</s> done to you, or what have I done, O you fixed on evil,
that you speak thus to me, doing what is hateful to all the world?
By doing only what is pleasing to you, I shall become much reviled.

children.text: yā tvaṃ bhāryā kālarātrī bharato nedṛśaḥ sutaḥ
children.translated_text: You are a wife who is a night of destruction; <s>Bharata</s> is not such a son.

children.text: praśādhi vidhavā rājyaṃ mṛte mayi gate sute ||
children.translated_text: Rule the kingdom as a widow, when I am dead and my son has gone.'
But bound by the noose of truth, he summoned <s>Rāma</s> and said:

children.text: kaikeyyā vañcito rāma rājyaṃ kuru nigṛhya mām ||
children.translated_text: 'I have been deceived by <s>Kaikeyī</s>, <s>Rāma</s>; take the kingdom, restraining me.

children.text: tvayā vane tu vastavyaṃ kaikeyībharato nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: Yet you must dwell in the forest; <s>Kaikeyī</s>'s <s>Bharata</s> is king.'
Having bowed to his father and to <s>Kaikeyī</s> and circumambulated them,

children.text: kṛtvā natvā ca kauśalyāṃ samāśvasya salakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: and having bowed to <s>Kauśalyā</s> and consoled her, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,
with his wife <s>Sītā</s>, with the chariot and with <s>Sumantra</s>,

children.text: dattvā dānāni viprebhyo dīnānāthebhya eva saḥ
children.translated_text: after giving gifts to brahmins and to the poor and helpless, he

children.text: mātṛbhiś caiva viprādyaiḥ śokārtair nirgataḥ purāt ||
children.translated_text: went out from the city, accompanied by his mothers, brahmins, and others, all stricken with grief.

children.text: uṣitvā tamasātīre rātrau paurān vihāya ca
children.translated_text: Having spent the night on the bank of the <s>Tamasā</s> and left the townspeople behind,
in the morning, not seeing him, they returned to <s>Ayodhyā</s>.
The weeping king, and <s>Kauśalyā</s> too, came home deeply distressed.

children.text: paurā janā striyaḥ sarvā rurudū rājayoṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The citizens, the people, all the women, and the king's wives wept.
<s>Rāma</s>, standing in the chariot and clad in bark, went to <s>Śṛṅgaverapura</s>.
Honored there by <s>Guha</s>, he stayed at the foot of an iṅgudī tree.

children.text: lakṣmaṇaḥ sa guho rātrau cakraturjāgaraṃ hi tau
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and that <s>Guha</s> kept watch through the night, those two.

children.text: sumantraṃ sarathaṃ tyaktvā prātar nāvātha jāhnavīṃ ||
children.translated_text: Leaving <s>Sumantra</s> with the chariot, in the morning by boat they crossed the <s>Jāhnavī</s>.
<s>Rāma</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and <s>Sītā</s>, having crossed, reached <s>Prayāga</s>.
After bowing to <s>Bharadvāja</s>, they went to Mount <s>Citrakūṭa</s>.
Then, having performed the house-site worship, they stayed on the bank of the <s>Mandākinī</s>.
<s>Rāghava</s> showed <s>Citrakūṭa</s> to <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: nakhair vidārayantaṃ tāṃ kākaṃ taccakṣur ākṣipat
children.translated_text: When a crow was tearing her with its claws, he struck out its eye.
With a reed-weapon it sought refuge, after abandoning the gods in the sky.

children.text: rāme vanaṃ gate rājā ṣaṣṭhe 'hni niśi cābravīt
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s> had gone to the forest, on the sixth day at night the king spoke

children.text: kauśalyāṃ sa kathāṃ paurvāṃ yadajñānaddhataḥ purā ||
children.translated_text: to <s>Kauśalyā</s> of that former story, how in the past he had killed unknowingly.
In his youth, on the bank of the <s>Sarayū</s>, the young <s>Yajñadatta</s>,

children.text: śabdabhedācca kumbhena śabdaṃ kurvaṃś ca tatpitā ||
children.translated_text: because of sound-piercing, was making a sound with a pot; and his father,
lamenting, together with the mother, cursed him, grieving and weeping again and again:

children.text: putraṃ vinā mariṣyāvas tvaṃ ca śokānmariṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: 'Without our son we shall die, and you too will die from grief.'

children.text: putraṃ vinā smaran śokāt kauśalye maraṇaṃ mama
children.translated_text: 'Without my son, remembering him from grief, O <s>Kauśalyā</s>, death is mine.'

children.text: kathāmuktvātha hā rāmam uktvā rājā divaṃgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having told the story, and crying 'Ah, <s>Rāma</s>!' the king went to heaven.

children.text: suptaṃ matvātha kauśalyā suptā śokārtameva sā
children.translated_text: Thinking him asleep, <s>Kauśalyā</s>, herself afflicted with grief, slept.
At daybreak the singers, charioteers, bards, and panegyrists,

children.text: prabodhakā bodhayanti na ca budhyatyasau mṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: the awakeners, tried to wake him; but he did not wake, for he was dead.

children.text: kauśalyā taṃ mṛtaṃ jñātvā hā hatāsmīti cābravīt ||
children.translated_text: Knowing him to be dead, <s>Kauśalyā</s> said, 'Ah, I am slain!'
Then men and women wept, and <s>Bharata</s> was brought at that time,
with <s>Śatrughna</s>, quickly from <s>Rājagṛha</s> to the city by <s>Vaśiṣṭha</s> and the others.
Seeing <s>Kaikeyī</s> in grief, he censured her, distressed.

children.text: akīrtiḥ pātitā mūrdhni kauśalyāṃ sa praśasya ca ||
children.translated_text: 'Infamy has been placed upon my head,' and he praised <s>Kauśalyā</s>.
Having performed the rites for his father, who lay in a vessel of oil, on the bank of the <s>Sarayū</s>,

children.text: vaśiṣṭhādyair janair ukto rājyaṃ kurviti so 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: he was told by <s>Vaśiṣṭha</s> and the others, and by the people, 'Rule the kingdom,' but he said:

children.text: vrajāmi rāmamānetuṃ rāmo rājā mato balī
children.translated_text: 'I am going to bring <s>Rāma</s> back. <s>Rāma</s> is considered the mighty king.'
Going to <s>Śṛṅgavera</s> and <s>Prayāga</s>, and fed by <s>Bharadvāja</s>,
after bowing to <s>Bharadvāja</s>, he came to <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: pitā svargaṃ gato rāma ayodhyāyāṃ nṛpo bhava ||
children.translated_text: 'Father has gone to heaven, <s>Rāma</s>; become king in <s>Ayodhyā</s>.
I shall go to the forest, awaiting your command.'

children.text: rāmaḥ śrutvā jalaṃ dattvā gṛhītvā pāduke vraja ||
children.translated_text: Having heard this, <s>Rāma</s> offered water and said, 'Take my sandals and go.
I shall not go for the kingdom; because of truth I wear bark and matted hair.'
Thus addressed by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Bharata</s> came back and stayed in <s>Nandigrāma</s>, mighty as he was.
Leaving <s>Ayodhyā</s>, he honored those sandals and governed the kingdom.

children.text: ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye rāmāyaṇe 'yodhyākāṇḍavarṇanaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the Āgneya Ādimahāpurāṇa, in the Rāmāyaṇa, the sixth chapter, named the Description of the Ayodhyākāṇḍa, is concluded.
<s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: rāmo vaśiṣṭhaṃ mātṝṃśca natvātiṃ ca praṇamya saḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, having bowed to <s>Vaśiṣṭha</s>, to his mothers, and to <s>Atri</s>,
and having bowed to <s>Anasūyā</s>, his wife, to <s>Śarabhaṅga</s>, and to <s>Sutīkṣṇa</s>,
and having bowed to <s>Agastya</s>'s brother and to <s>Agastya</s>, by his favor...
Having obtained a bow and sword, he came to the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest.
At <s>Janasthāna</s>, in <s>Pañcavaṭī</s>, he stayed on the bank of the <s>Godāvarī</s>.
There <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>, terrifying in form, came to devour them.

children.text: rāmaṃ surūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā sā kāminī vākyamabravīt
children.translated_text: Seeing handsome <s>Rāma</s>, that passionate woman spoke these words:

children.text: kastvaṃ kasmātsamāyāto bhartā me bhava cārthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Who are you? From where have you come? Become my husband, for I desire you.

children.text: etau ca bhakṣayiṣyāmi ity uktvā taṃ samudyatā
children.translated_text: And I shall devour these two.' Having said this, she rushed upon him.

children.text: tasyā nāsāṃ ca karṇau ca rāmokto lakṣmaṇo 'chinat ||
children.translated_text: At <s>Rāma</s>'s command, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> cut off her nose and ears.
Streaming blood, she went away and spoke to her brother <s>Khara</s>:

children.text: mariṣyāmi vinā sāhaṃ khara jīvāmi vai tadā ||
children.translated_text: 'Without that, O <s>Khara</s>, I shall die; only then shall I live.
<s>Sītā</s> is the wife of <s>Rāma</s>, and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> was his younger brother.

children.text: teṣām yadrudhiraṃ soṣṇaṃ pāyayiṣyasi māṃ yadi ||
children.translated_text: If you make me drink their hot blood,
<s>Khara</s> said to her, 'So be it,' and with fourteen thousand
rākṣasas, along with <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> and <s>Triśiras</s>, he went to fight.

children.text: rāmaṃ rāmo 'pi yuyudhe śarair vivyādha rākṣasān
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> too fought <s>Rāma</s>'s enemies and pierced the rākṣasas with arrows.
He sent the force of elephants, horses, chariots, and foot-soldiers to <s>Yama</s>'s abode.

children.text: triśīrṣāṇaṃ kharaṃ raudraṃ yudhyantaṃ caiva dūṣaṇam
children.translated_text: He killed <s>Triśiras</s>, fierce <s>Khara</s>, and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> as they fought.
<s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s> went to <s>Laṅkā</s> and fell on the ground before <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: abravīdrāvaṇaṃ kruddhā na tvaṃ rājā na rakṣakaḥ
children.translated_text: Angrily she said to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, 'You are no king and no protector.

children.text: kharādihantū rāmasya sītāṃ bhāryāṃ harasva ca ||
children.translated_text: Carry off <s>Sītā</s>, the wife of <s>Rāma</s>, the slayer of <s>Khara</s> and the others.
I shall live only by drinking the blood of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, not otherwise.'

children.text: tathetyāha ca tac chrutvā mārīcaṃ prāha vai vraja ||
children.translated_text: Hearing that, he said, 'So be it,' and then said to <s>Mārīca</s>, 'Go.
Become a golden, variegated deer and draw away <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: sītāgre tāṃ hariṣyāmi anyathā maraṇaṃ tava ||
children.translated_text: Before <s>Sītā</s> I shall carry her off; otherwise death is yours.'
<s>Mārīca</s> said to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, '<s>Rāma</s>, the bowman, is death itself.
One must die at <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s hands, and one must die at <s>Rāghava</s>'s hands.

children.text: avaśyaṃ yadi martavyaṃ varaṃ rāmo na rāvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: If death is inevitable, <s>Rāma</s> is preferable, not <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.'

children.text: iti matvā mṛgo bhūtvā sītāgre vyacaranmuhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thinking thus, he became a deer and repeatedly wandered before <s>Sītā</s>.
Urged on by <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Rāma</s> then killed him with an arrow.

children.text: mriyamāṇo mṛgaḥ prāha hā sīte lakṣmaṇeti ca ||
children.translated_text: As he was dying, the deer cried, 'Ah <s>Sītā</s>! Ah <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>!'
Then <s>Saumitri</s>, urged by <s>Sītā</s>, came to <s>Rāma</s>, though it was contrary to his judgment.
And <s>Rāvaṇa</s> carried off <s>Sītā</s>, after killing the vulture <s>Jaṭāyuṣa</s>.
His body torn by <s>Jaṭāyuṣa</s>, he took <s>Jānakī</s> on his lap
and went to <s>Laṅkā</s>; he kept her in the place called <s>Aśoka</s> and said:

children.text: bhava bhāryā mamāgryā tvaṃ rākṣasyo rakṣyatāmiyam
children.translated_text: 'Be my foremost wife. Let this woman be guarded by the rākṣasīs.'

children.text: rāmo hatvā tu mārīcaṃ dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇamabravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, after killing <s>Mārīca</s> and seeing <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, said:
'That was an illusory deer, O <s>Saumitri</s>, since you too have come here.

children.text: tathā sītā hṛtā nūnaṃ nāpaśyat sa gato 'tha tām ||
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>Sītā</s> has surely been carried off.' Then he went and did not see her.

children.text: śuśoca vilalāpārto māṃ tyaktvā kva gatāsi vai
children.translated_text: Afflicted, he grieved and lamented, 'Where have you gone, abandoning me?'
Comforted by <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, <s>Rāma</s> searched for <s>Jānakī</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā jaṭāyustaṃ prāha rāvaṇo hṛtavāṃś ca tāṃ
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Jaṭāyuṣa</s>, he was told by him, '<s>Rāvaṇa</s> has carried her off.'
Then <s>Jaṭāyuṣa</s> died and was given funeral rites by him; after that he killed <s>Kabandha</s>.
Released from his curse, he said to <s>Rāma</s>, 'You should approach <s>Sugrīva</s>.'

children.text: ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye rāmāyaṇe āraṇyakakāṇḍavarṇanaṃ nāma saptamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the Āgneya Ādimahāpurāṇa, the seventh chapter, named the description of the Araṇyakakāṇḍa in the Rāmāyaṇa, is concluded.
<s>Nārada</s> said:

children.text: rāmaḥ pampāsaro gatvā śocan sa śarvarīṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, having gone to lake <s>Pampā</s>, passed that night grieving.

children.text: hanūmatā sa sugrīvaṃ nīto mitraṃ cakāra ha ||
children.translated_text: Then, led by <s>Hanūmat</s> to <s>Sugrīva</s>, he made him his friend.
In his sight, with a single arrow, he pierced seven palm trees
and with his foot hurled the body of <s>Dundubhi</s> ten yojanas.
Having killed his enemy <s>Vālin</s>, his brother who had made hostility,

children.text: kiṣkindhāṃ kapirājyaṃ ca rumāṃ tārāṃ samarpayat ||
children.translated_text: he handed over <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, the monkey kingdom, and <s>Rumā</s> and <s>Tārā</s>.
On <s>Ṛṣyamūka</s>, the lord of the monkeys, now lord of <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>, said:

children.text: sītāṃ tvaṃ prāśyase yadvat tathā rāma karomi te ||
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Rāma</s>, I shall act for you so that you will obtain <s>Sītā</s>.'

children.text: tac chrutvā mālyavatpṛṣṭhe cāturmāsyaṃ cakāra saḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that, he spent the four rainy months on the back of <s>Mālyavat</s>.

children.text: kiṣkindhāyāṃ ca sugrīvo yadā nāyāti darśanaṃ ||
children.translated_text: But when <s>Sugrīva</s> in <s>Kiṣkindhā</s> did not come to see him,
then <s>Rāma</s> said to <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, 'Go to that <s>Rāghava</s>'s ally.

children.text: na sa saṃkucitaḥ panthā yena vālī hato gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The path by which <s>Vālin</s> was slain and went away is not blocked.

children.text: samaye tiṣṭha sugrīva mā vālipatham anvagāḥ
children.translated_text: Stand by the agreement, <s>Sugrīva</s>; do not follow <s>Vālin</s>'s path.'

children.text: sugrīva āha saṃsakto gataṃ kālaṃ na buddhavān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s> said, 'Attached to pleasure, I did not perceive that the time had passed.'

children.text: ityuktvā sa gato rāmaṃ natvovāca harīśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Saying this, the lord of the monkeys went to <s>Rāma</s>, bowed, and said:

children.text: ānītā vānarāḥ sarve sītāyāś ca gaveṣaṇe ||
children.translated_text: 'All the vānaras have been brought for the search for <s>Sītā</s>.
At your command I shall send them out; let them search for <s>Jānakī</s>.
Let them return within a month from the east and the other quarters; after more than a month I shall kill them.'
Thus instructed, the vānaras went along the eastern, western, and northern routes.

children.text: jagmū rāmaṃ sasugrīvam apaśyantas tu jānakīm ||
children.translated_text: Not seeing <s>Jānakī</s>, they returned to <s>Rāma</s> together with <s>Sugrīva</s>.
Taking <s>Rāma</s>'s ring, <s>Hanūmān</s>, together with the vānaras,
searched in the south near the cave of <s>Suprabhā</s>.

children.text: māsād ūrdhvaṃ ca vinyastā apaśyantastu jānakīm
children.translated_text: After more than a month had passed, not seeing <s>Jānakī</s>,
they said, 'We shall die in vain; <s>Jaṭāyuṣa</s> alone is blessed,

children.text: sītārthe yo 'tyajat prāṇān rāvaṇena hato raṇe
children.translated_text: for, killed by <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle, he gave up his life for <s>Sītā</s>.'

children.text: tac chrutvā prāha sampātir vihāya kapibhakṣaṇaṃ ||
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Sampāti</s>, giving up the thought of eating the monkeys, said:
'That <s>Jaṭāyuṣa</s> is indeed my brother. I flew up to the disk of the sun.
Protected by him from the sun's heat, I, whose wings were burned, fell from the sky.
Now, from hearing news of <s>Rāma</s>, my wings have grown again; and <s>Jānakī</s>,
I see, has gone to the Aśoka grove, in <s>Laṅkā</s> indeed.
On <s>Trikūṭa</s>, in the salt ocean, one hundred yojanas wide,

children.text: jñātvā rāmaṃ sasugrīvaṃ vānarāḥ kathayantu vai ||
children.translated_text: having learned this, let the vānaras tell <s>Rāma</s> together with <s>Sugrīva</s>.'

children.text: ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye rāmāyaṇe kiṣkindhākāṇḍavarṇanaṃ nāma aṣṭamo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth chapter, named the description of the Kiṣkindhākāṇḍa in the Rāmāyaṇa, in the Āgneya Ādimahāpurāṇa.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
After hearing the words of <s>Sampāti</s>, <s>Hanumān</s>, <s>Aṅgada</s>, and the others,

children.text: abdhiṃ dṛṣṭvābruvaṃste 'bdhiṃ laṅghayet ko nu jīvayet ||
children.translated_text: seeing the ocean, said, 'Who can leap across the ocean and remain alive?'
For the sake of the lives of the monkeys and for the accomplishment of <s>Rāma</s>'s task,
that son of the Wind leapt across the ocean, which was one hundred yojanas wide.

children.text: dṛṣṭvotthitaṃ ca mainākaṃ siṃhikāṃ vinipātya ca
children.translated_text: He saw <s>Maināka</s> rising up, and after striking down <s>Siṃhikā</s>,
he saw <s>Laṅkā</s>, the houses of the rākṣasas, and the women's quarters,
the houses of the ten-headed one, of <s>Kumbha</s>, and of the rākṣasa <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>,
of <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, of <s>Indrajit</s>, and of other rākṣasas.
Intent on anxious thought, he did not see <s>Sītā</s> in the drinking grounds and elsewhere.
Going to the aśoka grove, he saw her beneath a śiṃśapā tree:
<s>Sītā</s>, guarded by rākṣasī women, and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> saying, 'Become my wife,'

children.text: rāvaṇaṃ śiṃśapāstho 'tha neti sītāṃ tu vādinīṃ ||
children.translated_text: while he himself stayed in the śiṃśapā tree, and <s>Sītā</s> saying, 'No.'
The monkey heard the rākṣasī women saying, 'Become <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s wife.'

children.text: gate tu rāvaṇe prāha rājā daśaratho 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: But when <s>Rāvaṇa</s> had gone, he said, 'There was a king named <s>Daśaratha</s>.

children.text: rāmo 'sya lakṣmaṇaḥ putrau vanavāsaṃ gatau varau
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> are his two noble sons, who went into forest exile.

children.text: rāmapatnī jānakī tvaṃ rāvaṇena hṛtā balāt ||
children.translated_text: You are <s>Jānakī</s>, <s>Rāma</s>'s wife, carried off by force by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: rāmaḥ sugrīvamitras tvāṃ mārgayan preṣayacca mām
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, the friend of <s>Sugrīva</s>, is searching for you and has sent me.
Take this ring, given by <s>Rāma</s>, together with its token of recognition.'
<s>Sītā</s> took the ring, looking upon <s>Māruti</s> in return.

children.text: bhūyo 'gre copaviṣṭaṃ tam uvāca yadi jīvati ||
children.translated_text: Then, seeing him seated before her again, she said, 'If <s>Rāma</s> is alive,

children.text: rāmaḥ kathaṃ na nayati śṛṅki tām abravīt kapiḥ
children.translated_text: why does he not take me away?' The monkey said to that slender one:

children.text: rāmaḥ sīte na jānīte jñātvā tvāṃ sa nayiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Rāma</s> does not know; once he knows of you, he will take you away.

children.text: rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasaṃ hatvā sabalaṃ devi mā śuca
children.translated_text: After killing the rākṣasa <s>Rāvaṇa</s> together with his forces, O goddess, do not grieve.

children.text: sābhijñānaṃ dehi me tvaṃ maṇiṃ sītādadatkapau ||
children.translated_text: Give me a token of recognition.' <s>Sītā</s> gave a jewel to the monkey

children.text: uvāca māṃ yathā rāmo nayecchīghraṃ tathā kuru
children.translated_text: and said, 'Act so that <s>Rāma</s> may take me away quickly.
Go back, O remover of grief, with the story of the crow's attack on my eye.'
Taking the jewel and the story, <s>Hanumān</s> said, 'Your husband will take you away.

children.text: athavā te tvarā kācit pṛṣṭhamāruha me śubhe ||
children.translated_text: Or, if there is some urgency for you, climb onto my back, fair one.

children.text: adya tvāṃ darśayiṣyāmi sasugrīvaṃ ca rāghavam
children.translated_text: Today I shall show you <s>Rāghava</s> together with <s>Sugrīva</s>.'
<s>Sītā</s> said to <s>Hanumān</s>, 'Let <s>Rāghava</s> himself take me away.'
Then <s>Hanumān</s> devised a way to obtain sight of the ten-headed one.
He broke the grove, and after killing its guards with his teeth, nails, and the like,

children.text: hatvā tu kiṅkarān sarvān sapta mantrisutānapi
children.translated_text: and after killing all the kiṅkaras and also seven sons of ministers,

children.text: putramakṣaṃ kumāraṃ ca śakrajicca babandha tam ||
children.translated_text: as well as the prince <s>Akṣa</s>, <s>Śakrajit</s> bound him.
With a serpent-noose he bound the tawny-eyed one and showed him to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: uvāca rāvaṇaḥ kastvaṃ mārutiḥ prāha rāvaṇam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s> said, 'Who are you?' <s>Māruti</s> said to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>:
'I am <s>Rāma</s>'s messenger. Give <s>Sītā</s> to <s>Rāghava</s>, or you will die,

children.text: rāmabāṇair hataḥ sārdhaṃ laṅkāsthai rākṣasair dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: slain by <s>Rāma</s>'s arrows, certainly together with the rākṣasas dwelling in <s>Laṅkā</s>.'
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> was ready to kill him, but he was restrained by <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>.
He set fire to his tail, and <s>Māruti</s>, with his tail blazing,

children.text: dagdhvā laṅkāṃ rākṣasāṃś ca dṛṣṭvā sītāṃ praṇamya tām
children.translated_text: burned <s>Laṅkā</s> and the rākṣasas, saw <s>Sītā</s>, and bowed to her.
Having come back across the ocean, he said, '<s>Sītā</s> has been seen.'
With <s>Aṅgada</s> and the others, and among <s>Aṅgada</s>'s companions, they drank honey in the Honey-grove.

children.text: jitvā dadhimukhādīṃś ca dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ ca te 'bruvan ||
children.translated_text: After defeating <s>Dadhimukha</s> and the others, they saw <s>Rāma</s> and said:

children.text: dṛṣṭā sīteti rāmo 'pi hṛṣṭaḥ papraccha mārutim
children.translated_text: '<s>Sītā</s> has been seen.' <s>Rāma</s> too was delighted and asked <s>Māruti</s>:

children.text: kathaṃ dṛṣṭvā tvayā sītā kimuvāca ca māṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: 'How was <s>Sītā</s> seen by you, and what did she say concerning me?
Sprinkle me, who have entered the fire of longing, with the nectar of the tale of <s>Sītā</s>.'
<s>Hanumān</s> said to <s>Rāma</s>, 'I crossed the ocean and arrived there.

children.text: sītāṃ dṛṣṭvā purīṃ dagdhvā sītāmaṇiṃ gṛhāṇa vai
children.translated_text: After seeing <s>Sītā</s> and burning the city, take this jewel of <s>Sītā</s>.

children.text: hatvā tvaṃ rāvaṇaṃ sītāṃ prāpsyase rāma mā śuca ||
children.translated_text: After killing <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, you will obtain <s>Sītā</s>, O <s>Rāma</s>; do not grieve.'

children.text: gṛhītvā taṃ maṇiṃ rāmo ruroda virahāturaḥ
children.translated_text: Taking that jewel, <s>Rāma</s> wept, afflicted by separation.

children.text: maṇiṃ dṛṣṭvā jānakī me dṛṣṭā sītā nayasva mām ||
children.translated_text: 'Seeing the jewel, it is as though my <s>Jānakī</s> has been seen. <s>Sītā</s> has been seen; lead me to her.

children.text: tayā vinā na jīvāmi sugrīvādyaiḥ prabodhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Without her I cannot live.' He was consoled by <s>Sugrīva</s> and the others.
He went to the ocean shore. There <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> came to <s>Rāma</s>,
having been rejected by his evil-minded brother <s>Rāvaṇa</s>
when he had said, 'Give <s>Sītā</s> to <s>Rāma</s>.' He had no ally.
<s>Rāma</s> made <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> his friend and consecrated him to the sovereignty of <s>Laṅkā</s>.
When, as he entreated the ocean for a path, it did not come, then with arrows
he split it; and the ocean, having come, said to <s>Rāma</s>:

children.text: nalena setuṃ baddhvābdhau laṅkāṃ vraja gabhīrakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Having built a bridge over the ocean with <s>Nala</s>, go to deep <s>Laṅkā</s>.

children.text: ahaṃ tvayā kṛtaḥ pūrvaṃ rāmo 'pi nalasetunā
children.translated_text: I was made by you long ago.' Then <s>Rāma</s> too, by the bridge of <s>Nala</s>
made with trees, mountains, and the like, crossed to the far shore of the great ocean.

children.text: vānaraiḥ sa suvelasthaḥ saha laṅkāṃ dadarśa vai ||
children.translated_text: Standing on <s>Suvela</s> with the monkeys, he saw <s>Laṅkā</s>.

children.text: ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye rāmāyaṇe sundarakāṇḍavarṇanaṃ nāma navamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth chapter, named the description of the Sundarakāṇḍa in the Rāmāyaṇa, in the Āgneya Ādimahāpurāṇa.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
Commanded by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Aṅgada</s> went and said to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, '<s>Jānakī</s>
should be given quickly to <s>Rāghava</s>; otherwise you will die.'
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, whose rākṣasas were excited for battle, was ready to kill him.
The ten-headed one told <s>Rāma</s> that he considered only battle.

children.text: rāmo yuddhāya tac chrutvā laṅkāṃ sakapirāyayau
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Rāma</s> came to <s>Laṅkā</s> with the monkeys for battle.
The monkeys were <s>Hanumān</s>, <s>Mainda</s>, <s>Dvivida</s>, <s>Jāmbavān</s>, and <s>Nala</s>,
<s>Nīla</s>, <s>Tāra</s>, <s>Aṅgada</s>, <s>Dhūmra</s>, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, <s>Keśarī</s>, and <s>Gaya</s>,

children.text: panaso vinato rambhaḥ śarabhaḥ krathano balī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Panasa</s>, <s>Vinata</s>, <s>Rambha</s>, <s>Śarabha</s>, and mighty <s>Krathana</s>,
<s>Gavākṣa</s>, <s>Dadhivaktra</s>, <s>Gavaya</s>, and <s>Gandhamādana</s>.

children.text: ete cānye ca sugrīva etair yukto hy asaṃkhyakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Sugrīva</s>, together with these and countless others,
made the battle of the rākṣasas and vānaras appear confused and crowded.
The rākṣasas struck down the vānaras with arrows, spears, maces, and the like,
and the vānaras struck down the rākṣasas with nails, teeth, and rocks.
The force of the rākṣasas, with elephants, horses, chariots, and foot soldiers, was destroyed.
<s>Hanūmān</s> killed the enemy <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s> with a mountain peak.

children.text: akampanaṃ prahastaṃ ca yudhyantaṃ nīla āvadhīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nīla</s> killed <s>Akampana</s> and <s>Prahasta</s> as they fought.
<s>Rāma</s> and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, freed from the bondage of <s>Indrajit</s>'s arrows,
on seeing <s>Tārkṣya</s>, struck down the rākṣasa army with arrows.
In battle <s>Rāma</s> made <s>Rāvaṇa</s> shattered by his arrows.
And <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, distressed, awakened <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.
Then <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, awakened, drank a thousand jars
of liquor, ate buffaloes and the like, and said to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>:

children.text: sītāyā haraṇaṃ pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ tvaṃ hi gururyataḥ
children.translated_text: 'The abduction of <s>Sītā</s> was a sinful thing you have done, for you are the elder.

children.text: ato gacchāmi yuddhāya rāmaṃ hanmi savānaram ||
children.translated_text: Therefore I go to battle; I shall kill <s>Rāma</s> together with the vānaras.'

children.text: ityuktvā vānarān sarvān kumbhakarṇo mamarda ha
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> crushed all the vānaras.
<s>Sugrīva</s> was seized by him, but he cut off his ears and nose.
Deprived of ears and nose, he ate the vānaras.
Then <s>Rāma</s> cut off <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>'s arms with arrows.

children.text: tataḥ pādau tataśchittvā śiro bhūmau vyapātayat
children.translated_text: Then, after cutting off his feet, he made his head fall to the ground.

children.text: atha kumbho nikumbhaś ca makarākṣaś ca rākṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kumbha</s>, <s>Nikumbha</s>, and the rākṣasa <s>Makarākṣa</s>,
<s>Mahodara</s>, <s>Mahāpārśva</s>, the mad rākṣasa <s>Matta</s> and <s>Unmatta</s>,

children.text: praghaso bhāsakarṇaś ca virūpākṣaś ca saṃyuge ||
children.translated_text: <s>Praghasa</s>, <s>Bhāsakarṇa</s>, and <s>Virūpākṣa</s> in battle,
<s>Devāntaka</s>, <s>Narāntaka</s>, <s>Triśiras</s>, and <s>Atikāya</s>,
these, while fighting, were cast down on the earth by <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,

children.text: yudhyamānāstayā hy anye rākṣasā bhuvi pātitāḥ
children.translated_text: and the vānaras together with <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, as were other rākṣasas there.
<s>Indrajit</s>, fighting by means of illusion, bound <s>Rāma</s> and the others.
With serpent-arrows granted by a boon; but by the healing herb the two were made free of darts,
their wounds removed and healed, on the mountain brought by <s>Māruti</s>.
<s>Hanūmān</s> held up the mountain there where the herb was situated.

children.text: nikumbhilāyāṃ homādi kurvantaṃ taṃ hi lakṣmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, with arrows, struck down that heroic <s>Indrajit</s> in battle,

children.text: śarair indrajitaṃ vīraṃ yuddhe taṃ tu vyaśātayat
children.translated_text: while he was performing oblations and other rites at <s>Nikumbhilā</s>.
<s>Rāvaṇa</s>, scorched by grief, set out to kill <s>Sītā</s>.
Restrained by <s>Avindhya</s>, the king went forth in his chariot with his army.

children.text: indrokto mātalī rāmaṃ rathasthaṃ pracakāra tam ||
children.translated_text: At <s>Indra</s>'s command, <s>Mātalī</s> placed <s>Rāma</s> in a chariot.
The battle between <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was like a battle between <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> alone.

children.text: rāvaṇo vānarān hanti mārutyādyāś ca rāvaṇam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s> killed the vānaras, and <s>Māruti</s> and the others attacked <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: rāmaḥ śastraistamastraiś ca vavardha jalado yathā
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> increased against him with weapons and missiles, like a rain cloud.

children.text: tasya dhvajaṃ sa cicheda rathamaśvāṃś ca sārathim ||
children.translated_text: He cut down his banner, his chariot, his horses, and his charioteer,
as well as his bow, arms, and heads; yet his heads kept rising again.
After <s>Rāma</s> pierced his heart with the weapon of the grandsire,

children.text: bhūtale pātitaḥ sarvai rākṣasai ruruduḥ striyaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was cast down on the ground, and all the rākṣasa women wept.

children.text: āśvāsya taṃ ca saṃskṛtya rāmājñapto vibhīṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After consoling him and performing his funeral rites, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, commanded by <s>Rāma</s>,
had <s>Sītā</s> brought by <s>Hanūmān</s>; <s>Rāma</s> received her as pure.

children.text: rāmo vahnau praviṣṭāṃ tāṃ śuddhāmindrādibhiḥ stutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, praised by <s>Indra</s> and the others, accepted her as pure after she had entered the fire.
By <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Daśaratha</s> he was told, 'You are <s>Viṣṇu</s>, crusher of rākṣasas.'
<s>Indra</s>, worshiped by <s>Rāma</s>, revived the vānaras with a rain of nectar.

children.text: rāmeṇa pūjitā jagmur yuddhaṃ dṛṣṭvā divaṃ ca te
children.translated_text: Honored by <s>Rāma</s>, those who had seen the battle went also to heaven.
<s>Rāma</s> gave <s>Laṅkā</s> to <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> and honored the vānaras.

children.text: sasītaḥ puṣpake sthitvā gatamārgeṇa vai gataḥ
children.translated_text: Seated in the <s>Puṣpaka</s> with <s>Sītā</s>, he went back by the path by which he had come,
joyful in mind, showing <s>Sītā</s> the difficult forest regions.
After bowing to <s>Bharadvāja</s>, he arrived at <s>Nandigrāma</s>.
Bowed to by <s>Bharata</s>, he went to <s>Ayodhyā</s> and stayed there.
After bowing to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and the others, and to <s>Kauśalyā</s>, <s>Kaikeyī</s>,
and <s>Sumitrā</s>, having obtained the kingdom, he honored the twice-born and others.
Then he worshiped <s>Vāsudeva</s>, his own self, with aśvamedha sacrifices.

children.text: sarvadānāni sa dadau pālayāmāsa saḥ prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: He gave every kind of gift and protected his subjects
like sons, being devoted to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), desire, and the rest, and intent on restraining the wicked.
All people were devoted to every <s>dharma</s>, and the earth bore all crops.
There was no untimely death while <s>Rāma</s> ruled the kingdom.

children.text: ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye rāmāyaṇe yuddhakāṇḍavarṇanaṃ nāma daśamo 'dhyāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus in the primordial great Purāṇa, the Āgneya, in the Rāmāyaṇa, the tenth chapter, called 'The Description of the Yuddhakāṇḍa.'
<s>Nārada</s> said:
<s>Agastya</s> and the others, greatly honored, came to <s>Rāghava</s> as he sat in kingship.
'Blessed are you, victorious one, since <s>Indrajit</s> has been struck down.
<s>Pulastya</s> was a mind-born son of <s>Brahmā</s>; his son was <s>Viśravas</s>, and his wife was <s>Naikaṣī</s>.
<s>Puṣpotkaṭā</s> was the first; her son was <s>Dhaneśvara</s>.
From <s>Naikaṣī</s> was born <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, twenty-armed and ten-faced,
who by his austerity and by a boon given by <s>Brahmā</s> conquered the gods.
<s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> became one given to sleep, and <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> became righteous.
Their sister was <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>; <s>Meghanāda</s> was born from <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
After conquering <s>Indra</s> he became <s>Indrajit</s>, stronger than <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
He was killed by you through <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, while you sought the welfare of the gods and others.'

children.text: ityuktvā te gatā viprā agastyādyā namaskṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, those brahmins, <s>Agastya</s> and the others, were bowed to and departed.
At the gods' request and on <s>Rāma</s>'s command, <s>Śatrughna</s> became the destroyer of <s>Lavaṇa</s>.
There was formerly a certain <s>Mathurā</s>; at <s>Rāma</s>'s command, <s>Bharata</s> killed...
and three crores of the sons of <s>Śailūṣa</s> with sharp arrows.
The wicked gandharva <s>Śailūṣa</s>, who dwelt on the bank of the <s>Sindhu</s>,

children.text: takṣaṃ ca puṣkaraṃ putraṃ sthāpayitvātha deśayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, after installing his sons <s>Takṣa</s> and <s>Puṣkara</s> in the two regions,
<s>Bharata</s>, together with <s>Śatrughna</s>, went to <s>Rāghava</s>, honoring him, and remained there.
<s>Rāma</s>, having slain the wicked in battle and protected the good among men,
had two excellent sons, <s>Kuśa</s> and <s>Lava</s>, born in the hermitage of <s>Vālmīki</s>.
They became known from the report of their good conduct, while she had been abandoned because of public reproach.
Having consecrated them in the kingdom, he was intent on the meditation, 'I am <s>Brahman</s>.'
For ten thousand years and ten hundred years

children.text: rājyaṃ kṛtvā kratūn kṛtvā svargaṃ devārcito yayau
children.translated_text: he ruled the kingdom, performed sacrifices, and, honored by the gods, went to heaven,
together with the citizens, his younger brothers, <s>Sītā</s>'s sons, and the people of the country.
<s>Agni</s> said:
<s>Vālmīki</s>, having heard it from <s>Nārada</s>, composed the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>.
Whoever hears this account in full detail goes to heaven.

children.text: ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye rāmāyaṇe uttarakāṇḍavarṇanaṃ nāma ekādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eleventh chapter, named the description of the Uttarakāṇḍa in the Rāmāyaṇa, in the Āgneya Ādimahāpurāṇa.
<s>Agni</s> said:
I shall proclaim the <s>Harivaṃśa</s>. From the lotus of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s navel came the unborn one;
from <s>Brahmā</s> came <s>Atri</s>, then <s>Soma</s>; from <s>Soma</s> was born <s>Purūravas</s>.
From him came <s>Āyus</s>; from him <s>Nahuṣa</s>; after him was <s>Yayāti</s>.

children.text: yaduṃ ca turvasuṃ tasmād devayānī vyajāyata ||
children.translated_text: From him <s>Devayānī</s> bore <s>Yadu</s> and <s>Turvasu</s>.

children.text: druhyaṃ cānuṃ ca pūruṃ ca śarmiṣṭhā vārṣaparvaṇī
children.translated_text: <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, the daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>, bore <s>Druhyu</s>, <s>Anu</s>, and <s>Pūru</s>.
In the family of <s>Yadu</s> were the <s>Yādavas</s>, and <s>Vasudeva</s> was the best of them.
For the sake of removing the burden of the earth, from <s>Vasudeva</s> in <s>Devakī</s>
the six embryos, sons of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, were formerly brought by <s>Yoganidrā</s>,
sent by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, into the womb of <s>Devakī</s>.

children.text: abhūcca saptamo garbho devakyā jaṭharād balaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the seventh embryo, <s>Bala</s>, came to be transferred from <s>Devakī</s>'s womb
into <s>Rohiṇī</s>; thence he was called <s>Rauhiṇeya</s>. Then <s>Hari</s>,
on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s eighth lunar day in the month of <s>Nabhas</s>, at midnight, appeared four-armed.
Praised by <s>Devakī</s> and <s>Vasudeva</s>, the child became two-armed.
Out of fear of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, <s>Vasudeva</s> carried him to <s>Yaśodā</s>'s bed.
Taking <s>Yaśodā</s>'s little girl, he carried her to <s>Devakī</s>'s bed.

children.text: kaṃso bāladhvaniṃ śrutvā tāṃ cikṣepa śilātale ||
children.translated_text: Hearing the cry of the child, <s>Kaṃsa</s> hurled her onto a stone slab.
Although restrained by <s>Devakī</s>, he thought, 'This eighth embryo is my death.'
Hearing the bodiless voice, 'The embryos have been killed by me;
they had been handed over by <s>Devakī</s> at the time of her marriage, as foretold,'
that little girl, though hurled down, stood in the sky and said this to <s>Kaṃsa</s>:

children.text: kiṃ mayā kṣiptayā kaṃsa jāto yastvāṃ vadhiṣyati
children.translated_text: 'What use is there in throwing me down, O <s>Kaṃsa</s>? He who will kill you has been born.
He is the essence of all the gods, for the sake of removing the burden of the earth.'

children.text: ityuktvā sā ca śumbhādīn hatvendreṇa ca saṃstutā
children.translated_text: After saying this, she killed <s>Śumbha</s> and the others and was praised by <s>Indra</s>.
She is <s>Āryā</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Vedagarbhā</s>, <s>Ambikā</s>, and also <s>Bhadrakālī</s>,

children.text: bhadrā kṣemyā kṣemakarī naikabāhur namāmi tām
children.translated_text: <s>Bhadrā</s>, <s>Kṣemyā</s>, <s>Kṣemakarī</s>, and many-armed; I bow to her.
Whoever recites her names at the three junctions of the day obtains all desires.
<s>Kaṃsa</s> too sent <s>Pūtanā</s> and others for the destruction of the child.
The two, entrusted by <s>Vasudeva</s> to <s>Nanda</s>, the husband of <s>Yaśodā</s>,

children.text: rakṣaṇāya ca kaṃsāder bhītenaiva hi gokule
children.translated_text: for protection in <s>Gokula</s>, out of fear of <s>Kaṃsa</s> and the others,
<s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, wandered there with the cows and the cowherds.

children.text: sarvasya jagataḥ pālau gopālau tau babhūvatuḥ
children.translated_text: The two protectors of the whole world became cowherds.
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, bound to a mortar with a rope by agitated <s>Yaśodā</s>,
went between the twin arjuna trees, and the two arjuna trees were broken.
The cart too was overturned by the kick of his foot when he desired the breast.
<s>Pūtanā</s>, who had set out to kill him, was killed by his sucking at her breast.
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, gone to <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, defeated <s>Kāliya</s> from the pool of the <s>Yamunā</s>,
drove him out to the ocean, and, praised by <s>Bala</s>, made things secure.
He made the <s>Tālavana</s> safe by killing <s>Dhenuka</s>, the donkey.
He killed the bull <s>Ariṣṭa</s> and <s>Keśin</s>, who had the form of a horse.
Abandoning the festival of <s>Śakra</s>, he had a mountain-sacrifice performed.
By holding up the mountain, he warded off the rain sent by <s>Śakra</s>.
Then <s>Govinda</s> was honored by great <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Arjuna</s> was given to him.
The festival of <s>Indra</s>, however, was again performed by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> when he was pleased.
Standing in a chariot, praised by <s>Akrūra</s> at <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s command, he went to <s>Mathurā</s>,
watched by the loving gopīs with whom he had played.
Having killed the washerman who would not give them, he took the garments.

children.text: saha rāmeṇa mālābhṛn mālākāre varaṃ dadau
children.translated_text: Together with <s>Rāma</s>, wearing garlands, he gave a boon to the garland-maker.
He made straight the hunchback woman who had given him unguents, and killed the elephant,

children.text: mattaṃ kuvalayāpīḍaṃ dvāri raṅgaṃ praviśya ca
children.translated_text: the intoxicated <s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s>, at the gate; and after entering the arena,
while <s>Kaṃsa</s> and the others looked on from their seats, he engaged in wrestling.
He fought with the wrestler <s>Cāṇūra</s>, and <s>Bala</s> fought with <s>Muṣṭika</s>.
<s>Cāṇūra</s> and <s>Muṣṭika</s>, the wrestlers, and likewise the others, were killed by those two.
Having killed <s>Kaṃsa</s>, the lord of <s>Mathurā</s>, <s>Hari</s> made his father
king of the <s>Yādavas</s>; and <s>Asti</s> and <s>Prāpti</s> became the widows of <s>Kaṃsa</s>.
Those two daughters of <s>Jarāsandha</s> stirred up <s>Jarāsandha</s>.

children.text: cakre sa mathurārodhaṃ yādavair yuyudhe śaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He laid siege to <s>Mathurā</s> and fought with the <s>Yādavas</s> with arrows.
<s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, leaving <s>Mathurā</s>, came to <s>Gomanta</s>.
Having defeated <s>Jarāsandha</s> in battle, and <s>Pauṇḍraka Vāsudeva</s>,

children.text: purīṃ ca dvārakāṃ kṛtvā nyavasad yādavair vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: and having made the city <s>Dvārakā</s>, he dwelt there surrounded by the <s>Yādavas</s>.

children.text: bhaumaṃ tu narakaṃ hatvā tenānītāś ca kanyakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But after killing <s>Bhauma</s>, that is <s>Naraka</s>, the maidens who had been carried off by him,
belonging to the gods, gandharvas, and yakṣas, addressed <s>Janārdana</s>.
There were sixteen thousand women, and also eight beginning with <s>Rukmiṇī</s>.
Together with <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, <s>Hari</s>, the destroyer of <s>Naraka</s>, mounted on <s>Garuḍa</s>,

children.text: maṇiśailaṃ saratraṃ ca indraṃ jitvā harirdivi ||
children.translated_text: defeated <s>Indra</s> in heaven, along with <s>Maṇiśaila</s> and the guardians of the treasures.
Having brought the <s>Pārijāta</s>, he planted it in <s>Satyabhāmā</s>'s house.

children.text: sāṃdīpaneś ca śastrāstraṃ jñātvā tadbālakaṃ dadau ||
children.translated_text: And knowing the weapons and missiles of <s>Sāṃdīpani</s>, he gave back that teacher's boy.

children.text: jitvā pañcajanaṃ daityaṃ yamena ca supūjitaḥ
children.translated_text: After defeating the daitya <s>Pañcajana</s>, he was highly honored by <s>Yama</s>.
He slew <s>Kālayavana</s>, after being honored by <s>Mucukunda</s>.

children.text: vasudevaṃ devakīṃ ca bhaktaviprāṃś ca so 'rcayat
children.translated_text: He honored <s>Vasudeva</s>, <s>Devakī</s>, and the devoted brahmins.
From <s>Balabhadra</s>, in <s>Revatī</s>, were born <s>Niśaṭha</s> and <s>Ulmuka</s>.
From <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Śāmba</s> was born in <s>Jāmbavatī</s>, and other sons were born from other wives.
<s>Śambara</s> gave that fish to <s>Śambarā</s> and to <s>Māyāvatī</s>.
<s>Māyāvatī</s>, seeing her own husband inside the fish,

children.text: papoṣa sā taṃ covāca ratiste 'haṃ patirmama ||
children.translated_text: lovingly reared him and said to him, 'I am your <s>Rati</s>; you are my husband.
You are <s>Kāma</s>, made bodiless by <s>Śambhu</s>, and I have been carried off by <s>Śambara</s>.

children.text: hṛtā na tasya patnī tvaṃ māyājñaḥ śambaraṃ jahi ||
children.translated_text: You are not his wife; you know magic. Slay <s>Śambara</s>.'

children.text: tac chrutvā śambaraṃ hatvā pradyumnaḥ saha bhāryayā
children.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Pradyumna</s> killed <s>Śambara</s> and, together with his wife,

children.text: māyāvatyā yayau kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇo hṛṣṭo 'tha rukmiṇī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Māyāvatī</s>, went to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rukmiṇī</s> rejoiced.
From <s>Pradyumna</s> was born <s>Aniruddha</s>, noble-minded husband of <s>Uṣā</s>.
<s>Bāṇa</s>, son of <s>Bali</s>, had a daughter <s>Uṣā</s>; his city was <s>Śoṇita</s>.
By austerity he became as a son to <s>Śiva</s>, after the peacock-banner had fallen.

children.text: yuddhaṃ prāpsyasi bāṇa tvaṃ bāṇaṃ tuṣṭaḥ śivo 'bhyadhāt ||
children.translated_text: Pleased, <s>Śiva</s> said to <s>Bāṇa</s>, 'You will obtain a battle, O <s>Bāṇa</s>.'

children.text: śivena krīḍatīṃ gaurīṃ dṛṣṭvoṣā saspṛhā patau
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Gaurī</s> sporting with <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Uṣā</s> longed for a husband.

children.text: tāmāha gaurī bhartā te niśi supteti darśanāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gaurī</s> said to her, 'Your husband will be seen by you as you sleep at night.
On the twelfth day of the month of <s>Vaiśākha</s>, a man will become your husband.'

children.text: gauryuktā harṣitā coṣā gṛhe suptā dadarśa taṃ ||
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Gaurī</s>, delighted <s>Uṣā</s>, asleep in her house, saw him.
Learning that she had been united with him in herself, through her friend <s>Citralekhā</s>,
she brought <s>Aniruddha</s> from a painted picture on a cloth.
The daughter of <s>Kumbhāṇḍa</s>, <s>Bāṇa</s>'s minister, brought <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s grandson from <s>Dvārakā</s>.
<s>Aniruddha</s> came and sported with <s>Uṣā</s>.
By the fallings of <s>Bāṇa</s>'s banner he was reported by the guards.
There was a very terrible battle between <s>Aniruddha</s> and <s>Bāṇa</s>.
Hearing of it from <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with <s>Pradyumna</s> and <s>Balabhadra</s>,
mounted on <s>Garuḍa</s>, then conquered the fires and also the <s>Māheśvara</s> fever.
Then a battle of arrow against arrow arose between <s>Hari</s> and <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
<s>Nandin</s>, <s>Vināyaka</s>, <s>Skanda</s>, and the others were defeated by <s>Tārkṣya</s> and the rest.
When <s>Śaṅkara</s> yawned and was undone by <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s yawning weapon,
the thousand arms of <s>Bāṇa</s> were cut off, and safety was requested by <s>Rudra</s>.
Kept alive by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Bāṇa</s>, now two-armed, spoke to <s>Śiva</s>:

children.text: tvayā yadabhayaṃ dattaṃ bāṇasyāsya mayā ca tat ||
children.translated_text: 'The fearlessness that was given to this <s>Bāṇa</s> by you has been given by me also.

children.text: āvayor nāsti bhedo vai bhedī narakamāpnuyāt
children.translated_text: There is truly no difference between us two; one who sees difference goes to hell.'
Worshiped by <s>Śiva</s> and the others, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, together with <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Uṣā</s>, and the rest,
went to <s>Dvārakā</s> and sported there with <s>Ugrasena</s> and the other <s>Yādavas</s>.
<s>Vajra</s>, son of <s>Aniruddha</s>, became all-knowing through <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>.
<s>Balabhadra</s> became the slayer of <s>Pralamba</s> and the puller of the <s>Yamunā</s>.
He was the splitter of the monkey <s>Dvivida</s> and the destroyer of the arrogance of the Kauravas.
<s>Hari</s>, the lord, rejoiced in many forms with <s>Rukmiṇī</s> and the others.
He begot sons, those countless <s>Yādavas</s>.

children.text: harivaṃśaṃ paṭhet yaḥ sa prāptakāmo hariṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: Whoever recites the <s>Harivaṃśa</s>, having obtained his desires, will go to <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye harivaṃśavarṇanaṃ nāma dvādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twelfth chapter, called the description of the <s>Harivaṃśa</s>, in the Āgneya Ādimahāpurāṇa.
<s>Agni</s> said:
I shall declare the <s>Bhārata</s>, characterized by the greatness of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
<s>Viṣṇu</s> removed the burden of the earth, making the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> the occasion.
From <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s navel-lotus came <s>Brahmā</s>; <s>Atri</s> was a son of <s>Brahmā</s>.
From <s>Atri</s> came <s>Soma</s>, from <s>Soma</s> <s>Budha</s>, and from him was born <s>Purūravas</s>, the Aila.
From him came <s>Āyus</s>; then King <s>Nahuṣa</s>; after him came <s>Yayāti</s>.

children.text: tataḥ purustasya vaṃśe bharato 'tha nṛpaḥ kuruḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then came <s>Puru</s>; in his lineage were <s>Bharata</s>, and then King <s>Kuru</s>.
In that lineage was <s>Śāntanu</s>; from him came <s>Bhīṣma</s>, son of <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and two younger brothers,

children.text: citrāṅgado vicitraś ca satyavatyāṃ ca śāntanoḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Citrāṅgada</s> and <s>Vicitravīrya</s>, born from <s>Satyavatī</s> and <s>Śāntanu</s>.

children.text: svargaṃ gate śāntanau ca bhīṣmo bhāryāvivarjitaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Śāntanu</s> had gone to heaven, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, without a wife,
protected his brother's kingdom; the boy <s>Citrāṅgada</s> was killed.
Two maidens of the king of <s>Kāśī</s>, <s>Ambikā</s>
and <s>Ambālikā</s>, were brought by <s>Bhīṣma</s>, who had conquered his enemies.

children.text: bhārye vicitravīryasya yakṣmaṇā sa divaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: They became the wives of <s>Vicitravīrya</s>; he went to heaven through consumption.
With <s>Satyavatī</s>'s permission, in <s>Ambikā</s> a king was born.
From <s>Vyāsa</s> were born <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> in <s>Ambikā</s> and <s>Pāṇḍu</s> in <s>Ambālikā</s>.
From <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> in <s>Gāndhārī</s> came the hundred sons headed by <s>Duryodhana</s>.
At the hermitage called <s>Śataśṛṅga</s>, since death would come through union with his wives,
because of a seer's curse, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> was born from <s>Dharma</s> in <s>Kuntī</s> for <s>Pāṇḍu</s>.
<s>Bhīma</s> was born from <s>Vāta</s>, <s>Arjuna</s> from <s>Śakra</s>, and from the two <s>Aśvins</s> in <s>Mādrī</s>
were born <s>Nakula</s> and <s>Sahadeva</s>; <s>Pāṇḍu</s> died together with <s>Mādrī</s>.

children.text: karṇaḥ kuntyāṃ hi kanyāyāṃ jāto duryodhāśritaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Karṇa</s> had been born from <s>Kuntī</s> while she was still a maiden, and he took refuge with <s>Duryodhana</s>.
By the working of fate, enmity arose between the <s>Kurus</s> and the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>.
The evil-minded <s>Duryodhana</s> burned the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> in the lac house.
But the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, with their mother behind them, escaped from the burning house.
Then, in <s>Ekacakrā</s>, in the dwelling of a brahmin,
all of them stayed in the guise of sages, after killing the rākṣasa <s>Baka</s>.
They went to the land of the <s>Pañcālas</s>, to the svayaṃvara of <s>Draupadī</s>.
<s>Draupadī</s> was obtained by the five <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> through the piercing of the target by strength of arm.
Then they obtained half the kingdom and were recognized by <s>Duryodhana</s> and the others.
And <s>Arjuna</s> obtained the divine bow <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, an excellent chariot from <s>Pāvaka</s>,
and, in battle, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as his charioteer and inexhaustible arrows.
Likewise all of them, skilled in weapons, received the <s>brahmāstra</s> and other missiles from <s>Droṇa</s>.
With <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, that <s>Arjuna</s> satisfied <s>Agni</s> in the <s>Khāṇḍava</s> forest,
as the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> checked <s>Indra</s>'s rain with a shower of arrows.

children.text: jitā diśaḥ pāṇḍavaiś ca rājyaṃ cakre yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
children.translated_text: The quarters were conquered by the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, and <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> ruled the kingdom.

children.text: bahusvarṇaṃ rājasūyaṃ na sehe taṃ suyodhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Suyodhana</s> could not endure that rājasūya sacrifice rich in much gold.
Urged by his brother <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, by <s>Karṇa</s>, who had obtained prosperity,
and by <s>Śakuni</s> in the matter of dice, he defeated <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> at dice.
He won his kingdom, and, standing in the assembly, laughed because of an illusion.
Defeated, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, together with his brothers, went to the forest.
He passed the pledged twelve years in the forest,
feeding eighty-eight thousand twice-born men as before.
Then, with <s>Dhaumya</s> and with <s>Draupadī</s> as the sixth, he went to <s>Virāṭa</s>.

children.text: kaṅko dvijo hy avijñāto rājā bhīmo 'tha sūpakṛt ||
children.translated_text: Unrecognized, the king became the brahmin <s>Kaṅka</s>, and <s>Bhīma</s> became a cook.
<s>Arjuna</s> was <s>Bṛhannalā</s>, his wife was <s>Sairindhrī</s>, and so too the twins had other names.
Under another name <s>Bhīmasena</s> killed <s>Kīcaka</s> at night.
He killed that man who wished to carry off <s>Draupadī</s>; and <s>Arjuna</s> defeated the <s>Kurus</s>,

children.text: kurvato gograhādīṃś ca tair jñātāḥ pāṇḍavā atha ||
children.translated_text: who were making cattle-raids and the like. Then the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> were recognized by them.
<s>Subhadrā</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s sister, bore from <s>Arjuna</s>
<s>Abhimanyu</s>; and <s>Virāṭa</s> gave his daughter <s>Uttarā</s> to him.
That <s>Dharmarāja</s> became lord of seven akṣauhiṇīs for battle.
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having gone as envoy, spoke to the intolerant <s>Duryodhana</s>,
to king <s>Duryodhana</s>, lord then of eleven akṣauhiṇīs:

children.text: yudhiṣṭhirāyārdharājyaṃ dehi grāmāṃś ca pañca vā ||
children.translated_text: 'Give half the kingdom to <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, or even five villages.
