children.text: yudhyasva vā vacaḥ śrutvā kṛṣṇamāha suyodhanaḥ
children.translated_text: Or fight.' Hearing this speech, <s>Suyodhana</s> said to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:
'I will not give even land the size of a needle-point; I shall fight, intent on battle.'
Having shown his irresistible universal form, and honored by <s>Vidura</s>,
he went to <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> and said, 'Make war on this <s>Suyodhana</s>.'

children.text: ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye ādiparvādivarṇanaṃ nāma trayodaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, named 'The Description of the Ādi-parvan and the Following Books,' in the Āgneya Ādimahāpurāṇa.
<s>Agni</s> said:
The armies of <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> and <s>Duryodhana</s> went to <s>Kurukṣetra</s>.
Seeing <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, and the others, he did not fight, thinking, 'They are my teachers.'
The Blessed Lord said to <s>Pārtha</s>, 'Those headed by <s>Bhīṣma</s> are not to be grieved for.
Bodies are perishable; the embodied one does not perish.

children.text: ayamātmā paraṃ brahma ahaṃ brahmasmi viddhi tam
children.translated_text: This self is the supreme <s>brahman</s>; know it as 'I am <s>brahman</s>.'
The yogin is equal in success and failure. Uphold the <s>rājadharma</s> (royal duty).'
Then, addressed by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Arjuna</s> fought from his chariot amid the sound of instruments.
At first <s>Bhīṣma</s> became commander in the army of <s>Duryodhana</s>.

children.text: pāṇḍavānāṃ śikhaṇḍī ca tayoryuddhaṃ babhūva ha
children.translated_text: And <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> was among the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>; the battle between those two sides took place.
The sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, with <s>Bhīṣma</s>, struck down the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> in battle.
<s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> and the other <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> struck down the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> in combat.
A battle like that of gods and asuras arose between the armies of the <s>Kurus</s> and <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>.
As the gods watched at ease, it increased their delight.
For ten days <s>Bhīṣma</s> felled the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> army with missiles.

children.text: daśame hy arjuno bāṇair bhīṣmaṃ vīraṃ vavarṣa ha
children.translated_text: On the tenth day <s>Arjuna</s> showered the heroic <s>Bhīṣma</s> with arrows.
<s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, instructed by <s>Drupada</s>, rained weapons upon him like a cloud.
Elephants, horses, chariots, and foot-soldiers were struck down by one another's weapons.

children.text: bhīṣmaḥ svacchandamṛtyuś ca yuddhamārgaṃ pradarśya ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhīṣma</s>, whose death was at his own will, after showing the path of battle,
lay on a bed of arrows and, addressed by the <s>Vasus</s>, remained there for the world of the <s>Vasus</s>.

children.text: uttarāyaṇamīkṣaṃś ca dhyāyan viṣṇuṃ stavan sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Waiting for the northern course of the sun, he remained meditating on <s>Viṣṇu</s> and praising him.
When <s>Duryodhana</s> was afflicted with grief, <s>Droṇa</s> became commander.
In the delighted army of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> was commander.
A fierce battle took place between them, increasing the realm of <s>Yama</s>.
<s>Virāṭa</s>, <s>Drupada</s>, and the others sank in the ocean that was <s>Droṇa</s>.
The great army of <s>Duryodhana</s>, with elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry,
was led by <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>; <s>Droṇa</s> appeared like Time itself.
When it was said, '<s>Aśvatthāman</s> has been killed,' <s>Droṇa</s> cast aside his weapons.
Overwhelmed by the arrows of <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>, he fell upon the earth.
On the fifth day, hard to assail, after crushing all the kṣatriyas,
when <s>Duryodhana</s> was afflicted with grief, <s>Karṇa</s> became commander.

children.text: arjunaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca tayoryuddhaṃ babhūva ha
children.translated_text: And <s>Arjuna</s> was commander of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>; the battle between them took place.
It was weapon against weapon, very terrible, like the battle of gods and asuras.
In the battle called <s>Karṇa</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>, <s>Karṇa</s> killed enemies with arrows.
But on the second day <s>Karṇa</s> was struck down by <s>Arjuna</s>.

children.text: śalyo dinārdhaṃ yuyudhe hy avadhīttaṃ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śalya</s> fought for half a day, and <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> killed him.
With his army slain, <s>Suyodhana</s> fought with <s>Bhīmasena</s>.
After killing many men and others, he then spoke to <s>Bhīmasena</s>.

children.text: gadayā praharantaṃ tu bhīmastaṃ tu vyapātayat ||
children.translated_text: As he attacked with his mace, <s>Bhīma</s> struck him down.
With his mace he killed the other younger brothers of his on that eighteenth day.

children.text: rātrau suṣuptaṃ ca balaṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ nyapātayat ||
children.translated_text: At night, while it slept, the army of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> was struck down,
to the measure of an akṣauhiṇī, by the mighty <s>Aśvatthāman</s>.
He killed the sons of <s>Draupadī</s>, together with the <s>Pāñcālas</s>, and also <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>.
Then <s>Arjuna</s> took from him the head-jewel, while <s>Draupadī</s>, bereft of sons, was weeping.

children.text: śiromaṇiṃ tu jagrāha aiṣikāstreṇa tasya ca ||
children.translated_text: And he took his head-jewel by means of the aiṣika weapon.
<s>Hari</s> revived the embryo of <s>Uttarā</s>, which had been burned by <s>Aśvatthāman</s>'s weapon.
Then that child of <s>Uttarā</s>'s womb became king <s>Parīkṣit</s>.
<s>Kṛtavarman</s>, <s>Kṛpa</s>, and <s>Drauṇi</s>: these three escaped from the battle.

children.text: pāṇḍavāḥ sātyakiḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sapta muktā na cāpare ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, <s>Sātyaki</s>, and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: seven escaped, and no others.
After consoling the afflicted women, <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, together with <s>Bhīma</s> and the others,
performed the rites for the heroes who had been slain, and gave water, wealth, and other offerings.

children.text: bhīṣmāc chāntanavāc chrutvā dharmān sarvāṃś ca śāntidām
children.translated_text: Having heard from <s>Bhīṣma</s>, son of <s>Śantanu</s>, all the dharmas that bring peace,
the king became instructed in royal dharma, mokṣa dharma, and the dharma of gifts.
At the aśvamedha, the crusher of enemies gave gifts to the brahmins.
Having heard from <s>Arjuna</s> of the club-fight and the destruction of the <s>Yādavas</s>,
he installed <s>Parīkṣit</s> in the kingdom and, with his younger brothers, attained heaven.

children.text: ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye mahābhāratavarṇanaṃ nāma caturdaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the primordial great Purāṇa, the Āgneya, the fourteenth chapter, called 'The Description of the Mahābhārata.'
<s>Agni</s> said:
When <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> was established in kingship, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> went from one āśrama to another,

children.text: dhṛtarāṣṭro vanamagād gāndhārī ca pṛthā dvija ||
children.translated_text: and went to the forest, along with <s>Gāndhārī</s> and <s>Pṛthā</s>, O twice-born one.
<s>Vidura</s>, burned by a forest fire, went to heaven.
In this way <s>Viṣṇu</s> removed the burden of the earth, consisting of demons and the like.
For the sake of dharma and the destruction of adharma, he used the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> as instruments.
Under the pretext of a brahmin's curse, he removed his own clan with the club.
He consecrated <s>Vajra</s>, the burden-bearing descendant of the <s>Yādavas</s>, in the kingdom.

children.text: devadeśāt prabhāse sa dehaṃ tyaktvā svayaṃ hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, by divine command, <s>Hari</s> himself abandoned his body at <s>Prabhāsa</s>.
He is worshiped by the inhabitants of heaven in <s>Indra</s>'s world and in <s>Brahmā</s>'s world.
<s>Balabhadra</s>, whose form is <s>Ananta</s>, went to the subterranean world and heaven.

children.text: avināśī harirdevo dhyānibhir dhyeya eva saḥ
children.translated_text: The god <s>Hari</s> is imperishable; he alone is to be meditated upon by meditators.
Without him, the ocean flooded the site of <s>Dvārakā</s>.
<s>Pārtha</s> performed the rites for the <s>Yādavas</s>, giving water, wealth, and other offerings.

children.text: striyo 'ṣṭāvakraśāpena bhāryā viṣṇoś ca yāḥ sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The women, the wives of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who had remained there because of <s>Aṣṭāvakra</s>'s curse,
were again, through that very curse, carried off by cowherds armed with sticks.

children.text: arjunaṃ hi tiraskṛtya pārthaḥ śokaṃ cakāra ha ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, disregarding <s>Arjuna</s>, they were taken; and <s>Pārtha</s> grieved.
Consoled by <s>Vyāsa</s>, he understood, 'My strength existed in the presence of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.'
Having come to <s>Hastināpura</s>, <s>Pārtha</s> reported everything

children.text: yudhiṣṭhirāya sa bhrātre pālakāya nṛṇāṃ tadā
children.translated_text: to his brother <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, who was then the protector of men.

children.text: taddhanustāni cāstrāṇi sa rathaste ca vājinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That bow, those weapons, that chariot, and those horses,

children.text: vinā kṛṣṇena tannaṣṭaṃ dānaṃ cāśrotriye yathā
children.translated_text: without <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, had been lost, like a gift given to one unfit to hear the Veda.
Hearing this, <s>Dharmarāja</s> installed <s>Parīkṣit</s> in the kingdom.

children.text: prasthānaṃ prasthito dhīmān draupadyā bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
children.translated_text: The wise one set out on the great departure, together with <s>Draupadī</s> and his brothers.
Knowing the impermanence of saṃsāra, he recited the eight hundred names of <s>Hari</s>.
On the great road fell <s>Draupadī</s>, <s>Sahadeva</s>,
<s>Nakula</s>, <s>Phālguna</s>, and <s>Bhīma</s>, while the king was overcome with grief.
Mounted on the chariot brought by <s>Indra</s>, he attained heaven with his younger brothers.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā duryodhanādīṃś ca vāsudevaṃ ca harṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Duryodhana</s> and the others, and <s>Vāsudeva</s>, he rejoiced.

children.text: etatte bhārataṃ proktaṃ yaḥ paṭhetsa divaṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Bhārata</s> has been told to you; whoever recites it goes to heaven.

children.text: ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye mahābhāratavarṇanaṃ nāma pañcadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the primordial great Purāṇa, the Āgneya, the fifteenth chapter, called 'The Description of the Mahābhārata.'
<s>Agni</s> said:
I shall describe the Buddha incarnation, which grants benefit to one who recites or hears it.

children.text: purā devāsure yuddhe daityair devāḥ parājitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Formerly, in a war between the gods and demons, the gods were defeated by the daityas.
Saying, 'Protect us, protect us,' they went to <s>Īśvara</s> for refuge.
He, whose form was deluding illusion, became the son of <s>Śuddhodana</s>.
He deluded those daityas and caused them to abandon Vedic dharma.

children.text: te ca bauddhā babhūvurhi tebhyo 'nye vedavarjitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They became Buddhists, and others apart from them became devoid of the Veda.
Afterward he became an Arhat, and made others into Arhats.
In this way heretics arose, bereft of Vedic dharma and the like.
They performed deeds worthy of hell, and they will accept teaching even from the lowest.

children.text: sarve kaliyugānte tu bhaviṣyanti ca saṅkarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the end of the Kali age, all people will become mixed in caste.
They will be robbers and devoid of good conduct; the Vājasaneyi Veda

children.text: daśa pañca ca śākhā vai pramāṇena bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will remain authoritative in only fifteen branches.
Clothed in the cloak of dharma, yet delighting in adharma,
mlecchas in the form of kings will devour human beings.
<s>Kalki</s>, son of <s>Viṣṇuyaśas</s>, with <s>Yājñavalkya</s> as his priest,
will destroy the mlecchas, taking up weapons and preparing for battle.
He will establish the proper boundaries in the four varṇas,
and among all the āśramas he will set the subjects on the path of true dharma.
Having abandoned the form of <s>Kalki</s>, <s>Hari</s> will go to heaven.
Then the age called Kṛta will arise again, as before.

children.text: varṇāśramāś ca dharmeṣu sveṣu sthāsyanti sattama
children.translated_text: The varṇas and āśramas will abide in their own dharmas, O best one.
Thus in all kalpas and in all manvantaras
the avatāras of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, past and future and the rest, are countless.
A person who recites or hears the accounts called the ten avatāras of <s>Viṣṇu</s>
obtains his desires, becomes stainless, and reaches heaven together with his family.
In this way <s>Hari</s> indeed establishes the ordering of dharma and adharma.

children.text: avatīrṇaṃ ca sa gataḥ sargādeḥ kāraṇaṃ hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having descended, <s>Hari</s>, the cause of creation and the rest, has departed.

children.text: ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye buddhakalkyavatāravarṇanaṃ nāma ṣoḍaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the primordial great Purāṇa, the Āgneya, the sixteenth chapter, called 'The Description of the Buddha and Kalki Incarnations.'
<s>Agni</s> said:
Now I shall tell of the playful acts of <s>Viṣṇu</s> beginning with the creation of the world; listen.
He is the maker of heaven and the rest, the source of creation and the like, both creation and its continuance, possessed of qualities and yet without qualities.
In the beginning there was always the unmanifest <s>Brahman</s>; there was no space, no night or day, and so on.
Then <s>Viṣṇu</s>, entering prakṛti and puruṣa, stirred them.
At the time of creation the great principle came into being, and from it arose ahaṅkāra.
It was vaikārika, taijasa, and also bhūtādi, the tāmasa form.
From ahaṅkāra came the mere element of sound, and from that came space.
From that came air, whose subtle element is touch; from that came fire, whose subtle element is form.

children.text: rasamātrā āpa ito gandhamātrā mahī smṛtā
children.translated_text: From this came the waters, whose subtle element is taste; earth is remembered as having smell as its subtle element.
From tāmasa ahaṅkāra, and also from taijasa, came the sense faculties.
From vaikārika came the ten deities, and the mind as the eleventh sense faculty.
Then the blessed <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>, wishing to create various creatures,
first created the waters, and into them he released his seed.

children.text: āpo nārā iti proktā āpo vai narasūnavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The waters are called nārā; indeed, the waters are the offspring of <s>Nara</s>.

children.text: ayanaṃ tasya tāḥ pūrvaṃ tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: They were formerly his resting-place; therefore he is remembered as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
Then there came into being a golden-colored egg lying in the water.

children.text: tasmin jajñe svayaṃ brahmā svayambhūriti naḥ śrutam
children.translated_text: In it <s>Brahmā</s> himself was born, as we have heard, and he is called <s>Svayambhū</s>.
The blessed <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, after dwelling there for a full year,
divided that egg in two, making heaven and also earth.
Between those two halves the lord created space.

children.text: apsu pāriplavāṃ pṛthivīṃ diśaś ca daśadhā dadhe
children.translated_text: He set the floating earth upon the waters, and arranged the directions in ten divisions.

children.text: tatra kālaṃ mano vācaṃ kāmaṃ krodhamatho ratim ||
children.translated_text: There he created time, mind, speech, desire, anger, and also pleasure.
<s>Prajāpati</s>, wishing to create beings, created a creation of that form.
He created lightning, thunderbolts, clouds, red rainbows,

children.text: vayāṃsi ca sasarjādau parjanyaṃ cātha vaktrataḥ
children.translated_text: and birds at the beginning, and then rain from his mouth.
For the accomplishment of sacrifice he fashioned the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman hymns.
With those the Sādhyas sacrificed to the gods; from his arms he created high and low beings.
He created <s>Sanatkumāra</s> and <s>Rudra</s>, born from anger.
He created <s>Marīci</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, and <s>Kratu</s>,

children.text: vasiṣṭhaṃ mānasāḥ sapta brahmāṇa iti niścitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>; these seven are certainly the mind-born sons of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: saptaite janayanti sma prajā rudrāś ca sattama
children.translated_text: These seven, and the Rudras too, O best one, generated creatures.
Dividing his own body in two, with one half he became male,

children.text: ardhena nārī tasyāṃ sa brahmā vai cāsṛjat prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and with one half female; in her <s>Brahmā</s> indeed created creatures.

children.text: ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye jagatsargavarṇanaṃ nāma saptadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the primordial great Purāṇa, the Āgneya, the seventeenth chapter, called 'The Description of the Creation of the World.'
<s>Agni</s> said:
<s>Priyavrata</s> and <s>Uttānapāda</s> were the two sons of <s>Svāyambhuva Manu</s>.
He begot that daughter <s>Śatarūpā</s>, endowed with austerity.
From <s>Kāmyā</s>, the wife of <s>Kardama</s>, came <s>Samrāṭ</s>, <s>Kukṣi</s>, <s>Virāṭ</s>, and <s>Prabhu</s>.
In <s>Suruci</s>, a son named <s>Uttama</s> was born from <s>Uttānapāda</s>.

children.text: sunītyāṃ tu dhruvaḥ putrastapastepe sa kīrtaye
children.translated_text: But in <s>Sunīti</s> a son, <s>Dhruva</s>, was born; he performed austerity for the sake of fame.

children.text: dhruvo varṣasahasrāṇi trīṇi divyāni he mune ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dhruva</s> practiced austerity for three thousand divine years, O sage.

children.text: tasmai prīto hariḥ prādānmunyagre sthānakaṃ sthiram
children.translated_text: Pleased with him, <s>Hari</s> gave him a fixed place before the sages.

children.text: ślokaṃ papāṭha hy uśanā vṛddhiṃ dṛṣṭvā sa tasya ca ||
children.translated_text: Seeing his greatness, <s>Uśanas</s> recited a verse about him:
'Ah, the power of his austerity! Ah, his learning! Ah, how wondrous he is!

children.text: yamadya purataḥ kṛtvā dhruvaṃ saptarṣayaḥ sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Putting him before them today, the seven seers stand fixed around <s>Dhruva</s>.'

children.text: tasmāt śiṣṭiṃ ca bhavyaṃ ca dhruvācchambhurvyajāyata
children.translated_text: From <s>Dhruva</s> were born <s>Śiṣṭi</s> and <s>Bhavya</s>, and from <s>Dhruva</s> <s>Śambhu</s> came forth.
From <s>Śiṣṭi</s>, <s>Succhāyā</s> bore five stainless sons:
<s>Ripu</s>, <s>Ripuñjaya</s>, <s>Ripra</s>, <s>Vṛkala</s>, and <s>Vṛkatejas</s>.
To <s>Ripu</s>, <s>Bṛhatī</s> bore <s>Cākṣuṣa</s>, who was full of every splendor.
He begot <s>Cākṣuṣa Manu</s> in <s>Puṣkariṇī</s>, also called <s>Vīriṇī</s>.
From that Manu, by <s>Naḍvalā</s>, ten excellent sons were born:
<s>Ūru</s>, <s>Puru</s>, <s>Śatadyumna</s>, <s>Tapasvī</s>, <s>Satyavāk</s>, and <s>Kavi</s>,
<s>Agniṣṭut</s>, <s>Atirātra</s>, <s>Sudyumna</s>, and <s>Abhimanyuka</s>.
From <s>Ūru</s>, <s>Āgneyī</s> bore six sons of great splendor:

children.text: aṅgaṃ sumanasaṃ svātiṃ kratum aṅgirasaṃ gayam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aṅga</s>, <s>Sumanas</s>, <s>Svāti</s>, <s>Kratu</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, and <s>Gaya</s>.
From <s>Aṅga</s>, as the offspring of <s>Sunīthā</s>, one son, <s>Veṇa</s>, was born.

children.text: arakṣakaḥ pāparataḥ sa hato munibhiḥ kuśaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He was no protector and delighted in evil; he was killed by the sages with kuśa-grass.
Then, for the sake of the subjects, the seers churned his right hand.

children.text: veṇasya mathito pāṇau saṃbabhūva pṛthur nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Veṇa</s>'s hand was churned, King <s>Pṛthu</s> came into being.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā munayaḥ prāhureṣa vai muditāḥ prajāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing him, the sages joyfully said, 'This man, of great splendor,

children.text: kariṣyati mahātejā yaśaś ca prāpsyate mahat ||
children.translated_text: will make the subjects prosper, and he will attain great fame.'
He was born with bow and armor, as if burning with his brilliance.

children.text: pṛthur vainyaḥ prajāḥ sarvā rarakṣa kṣetrapūrvajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pṛthu Vainya</s>, the firstborn in the field, protected all the subjects.
He was the first lord of the earth among those consecrated by the rājasūya.
From him also arose two skillful men, a sūta and a māgadha.
Those two heroes composed his praise; he became king because he delighted the people.

children.text: dugdhā gaustena śasyārthaṃ prajānāṃ jīvanāya ca ||
children.translated_text: By him the cow was milked for grain, for the livelihood of the subjects.
Together with the gods, groups of sages, gandharvas, and companies of apsarases,
with the ancestors, dānavas, serpents, plants, mountains, and human beings,

children.text: teṣu teṣu ca pātreṣu duhyamānā vasundharā
children.translated_text: the earth, being milked into each of their vessels,
gave the desired milk to each; by that he sustained their lives.
Two sons, knowers of dharma, were born to <s>Pṛthu</s>, ruling the inner islands.
From <s>Antardhāna</s> were born <s>Śikhaṇḍī</s> and <s>Havirdhāna</s>.
From <s>Havirdhāna</s>, <s>Dhīṣaṇā</s>, the Āgneyī, bore six sons:
<s>Prācīnabarhis</s>, <s>Śukra</s>, <s>Gaya</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Vraja</s>, and <s>Ajina</s>.
Because the tips of his <s>kuśa</s> grass faced east as he sacrificed on the earth,
that blessed great <s>Prajāpati</s> was called <s>Prācīnabarhis</s>.
<s>Sāmudrī</s>, of the same class, bore ten sons to <s>Prācīnabarhis</s>.
All were named the <s>Pracetas</s>, masters of the science of archery.
Practicing <s>dharma</s> without division, they performed great austerity,
lying in the water of the ocean for ten thousand years.

children.text: prajāpatitvaṃ samprāpya tuṣṭā viṣṇoś ca nirgatāḥ
children.translated_text: Having obtained the office of <s>Prajāpati</s>, and having emerged, satisfied, from <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: bhūḥ khaṃ vyāptaṃ hi tarubhistāṃstarūnadahaṃś ca te ||
children.translated_text: they found the earth and sky covered with trees, and they burned those trees.
Seeing the destruction of the trees by the fire and wind from their mouths,
King <s>Soma</s> approached and then spoke to those <s>Prajāpatis</s>:

children.text: kopaṃ yacchata dāsyanti kanyāṃ vo māriṣāṃ varām
children.translated_text: 'Restrain your anger. They will give you the excellent maiden <s>Māriṣā</s>,

children.text: tapasvino muneḥ kaṇḍoḥ pramlocāyāṃ mamaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: born of the ascetic sage <s>Kaṇḍu</s>, of <s>Pramlocā</s>, and indeed of myself.

children.text: bhaviṣyaṃ jānatā sṛṣṭā bhāryā vo 'stu kulaṃkarī
children.translated_text: Created by one who knew the future, let her be your wife, increasing your family.
From her <s>Dakṣa</s> will be born, and he will cause creatures to increase.'
The <s>Pracetas</s> took her, and then <s>Dakṣa</s> was born from her.

children.text: acarāṃś ca carāṃś caiva dvipado 'tha catuṣpadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He created both unmoving and moving beings, two-footed and four-footed.

children.text: sa sṛṣṭvā manasā dakṣaḥ paścādasṛjata striyaḥ
children.translated_text: Having created them mentally, <s>Dakṣa</s> afterward created women.

children.text: dadau sa daśa dharmāya kaśyapāya trayodaśa ||
children.translated_text: He gave ten to <s>Dharma</s> and thirteen to <s>Kaśyapa</s>.
He gave twenty-seven to <s>Soma</s> and four to <s>Ariṣṭanemi</s>;

children.text: dve caiva bahuputrāya dve caivāṅgirase adāt ||
children.translated_text: he gave two to <s>Bahuputra</s> and two to <s>Aṅgiras</s>.

children.text: tāsu devāś ca nāgādyā maithunānmanasā purā
children.translated_text: From them, in ancient times, gods, serpents, and others were born by sexual union and by mind.
I shall duly declare the creation by <s>Dharma</s> through his ten wives.
From <s>Viśvā</s> came the <s>Viśvedevas</s>; <s>Sādhyā</s> gave birth to the <s>Sādhyas</s>.
From <s>Marutvatī</s> came the <s>Marutvants</s>, and from <s>Vasu</s> the <s>Vasus</s> arose.
From <s>Bhānu</s> came the sons called <s>Bhānus</s>; from <s>Muhūrtā</s> came those born of the moments.

children.text: sambāyā dharmato ghoṣo nāgavīthī ca yāmijā ||
children.translated_text: From <s>Sambā</s>, through <s>Dharma</s>, came <s>Ghoṣa</s>; and <s>Nāgavīthī</s> was born of <s>Yāmī</s>.
Everything belonging to the earthly realm was born from <s>Arundhatī</s>.
From <s>Saṃkalpā</s> came the <s>Saṃkalpas</s>; the sons of <s>Indu</s> were the lunar mansions.

children.text: āpo dhruvaṃ ca somaṃ ca dharaś caivānilo 'nalaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Āpa</s>, <s>Dhruva</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Dhara</s>, <s>Anila</s>, <s>Anala</s>,

children.text: pratyūṣaś ca prabhāvaś ca vasavo 'ṣṭau ca nāmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pratyūṣa</s>, and <s>Prabhāva</s>: these are the eight <s>Vasus</s> by name.

children.text: āpasya putro vaitaṇḍyaḥ śramaḥ śānto munis tathā
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Āpa</s> was <s>Vaitaṇḍya</s>; also <s>Śrama</s>, <s>Śānta</s>, and <s>Muni</s>.

children.text: dhruvasya kālo lokānto varcāḥ somasya vai sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Dhruva</s> was <s>Kāla</s>, the end of the worlds; <s>Varcas</s> was the son of <s>Soma</s>.
The son of <s>Dhara</s> was <s>Draviṇa</s>, and also <s>Hutahavyavaha</s>.
From <s>Manoharā</s> came <s>Śiśira</s>, then <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Ramaṇa</s>.
<s>Purojava</s> was born from <s>Anila</s>, and <s>Avijñāta</s> from <s>Anala</s>.
The fire-born son was <s>Kumāra</s>, born in a clump of reeds.

children.text: tasya śākho viśākhaś ca naigameyaś ca pṛṣṭhajaḥ
children.translated_text: His sons were <s>Śākha</s>, <s>Viśākha</s>, and <s>Naigameya</s>, born from his back.
From the <s>Kṛttikās</s> came <s>Kārttikeya</s>, <s>Yati</s>, and little <s>Sanatkumāra</s>.
From <s>Pratyūṣa</s> was born <s>Devala</s>; from <s>Prabhāva</s>, <s>Viśvakarmā</s>,
the maker of thousands of crafts and the carpenter of the thirty gods.
Human beings too live by crafts, such as ornaments and the like.
<s>Surabhī</s>, through <s>Kaśyapa</s>, gave birth to the eleven <s>Rudras</s>.
She was a virtuous woman purified by austerity through the favor of <s>Mahādeva</s>.

children.text: ajaikapād ahir bradhnas tvaṣṭā rudrāś ca sattama ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ajaikapād</s>, <s>Ahirbradhna</s>, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, and the <s>Rudras</s>, O best of beings,
and the glorious, very famous <s>Viśvarūpa</s>, son of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>;
<s>Hara</s>, <s>Bahurūpa</s>, <s>Tryambaka</s>, and <s>Aparājita</s>;

children.text: vṛṣākapiś ca śambhuś ca kapardī raivatas tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Kapardī</s>, and <s>Raivata</s>;

children.text: mṛgavyādhasya sarpaś ca kapālī daśa caikakaḥ
children.translated_text: the son of <s>Mṛgavyādha</s>, <s>Sarpa</s>, <s>Kapālī</s>, and the eleventh, <s>Ekaka</s>.

children.text: rudrāṇāṃ ca śataṃ lakṣaṃ yair vyāptaṃ sacarācaraṃ ||
children.translated_text: There are a hundred thousand <s>Rudras</s>, by whom the moving and unmoving universe is pervaded.

children.text: ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye jagatsargavarṇanaṃ nāma aṣṭādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the primordial great Purāṇa, the Āgneya, the eighteenth chapter, called 'The Description of the Creation of the World.'
<s>Agni</s> said:
O sage, learn the creation of <s>Kaśyapa</s> among <s>Aditi</s> and the others.
In the <s>Cākṣuṣa</s> age the gods were the <s>Tuṣitas</s>; they were again born from <s>Aditi</s> and <s>Kaśyapa</s>.

children.text: āsan viṣṇuś ca śakraś ca tvaṣṭā dhātā tathāryamā
children.translated_text: They were <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, <s>Dhātṛ</s>, and also <s>Aryaman</s>,

children.text: pūṣā vivasvān savitā mitro 'tha varuṇo bhagaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Vivasvān</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, then <s>Varuṇa</s> and <s>Bhaga</s>.
And <s>Aṃśu</s>: these were the twelve <s>Ādityas</s> in the <s>Vaivasvata</s> interval.
Here the offspring of the wives of <s>Ariṣṭanemi</s> were sixteen.
The four daughters of <s>Bahuputra</s> were the wise <s>Vidyuts</s>.
The excellent sons born from <s>Pratyaṅgirā</s> were the divine weapons of <s>Kṛśāśva</s>.
Like the rising and setting of the sun, these recur age after age.
From <s>Diti</s> and <s>Kaśyapa</s> came <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> and <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>.
And <s>Siṃhikā</s> was their daughter; she became the wife of <s>Vipracitti</s>.
From her came <s>Rāhu</s> and the others, who are known as the <s>Saiṃhikeyas</s>.
The sons of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> were four, renowned for their power:
<s>Anuhrāda</s>, <s>Hrāda</s>, and <s>Prahrāda</s>, who was exceedingly devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: saṃhrādaś ca caturtho 'bhūt hrādaputro hradas tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃhrāda</s> was the fourth; likewise <s>Hrada</s> was the son of <s>Hrāda</s>.

children.text: hradasya putra āyuṣmān śibir bāskala eva ca ||
children.translated_text: The sons of <s>Hrada</s> were long-lived <s>Śibi</s> and <s>Bāskala</s>.
<s>Virocana</s> was the son of <s>Prahrāda</s>, and <s>Bali</s> was born from <s>Virocana</s>.
<s>Bali</s> had a hundred sons, O great sage, with <s>Bāṇa</s> as the foremost.
In an earlier age, <s>Bāṇa</s>, having pleased the husband of <s>Umā</s>, received a boon:
'I shall sport at your side'; thus it was obtained from <s>Īśvara</s>.
The sons of <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> were five: <s>Śambara</s>, <s>Śakuni</s>,

children.text: dvimūrdhā śaṅkurāryaś ca śatamāsan danoḥ sutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dvimūrdhā</s>, <s>Śaṅku</s>, and <s>Ārya</s>; and the sons of <s>Danu</s> were a hundred.

children.text: svarbhānostu prabhā kanyā pulomnastu śacī smṛtā
children.translated_text: The daughter of <s>Svarbhānu</s> was <s>Prabhā</s>; <s>Śacī</s> is remembered as the daughter of <s>Puloman</s>.
<s>Upadānavī</s>, <s>Hayaśirā</s>, and <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> were daughters of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>.
<s>Pulomā</s> and <s>Kālakā</s> were both daughters of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.

children.text: kaśyapasya tu bhārye dve tayoḥ putrāś ca koṭayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But <s>Kaśyapa</s> had two wives, and their sons were in the tens of millions.
In the line of <s>Prahrāda</s> there were four crores, the <s>Nivātakavacas</s>.

children.text: tāmrāyāḥ ṣaṭ sutāḥ syuś ca kākī śvenī ca bhāsyapi ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Tāmrā</s> had six daughters: <s>Kākī</s>, <s>Śyenī</s>, and <s>Bhāsī</s>,
<s>Gṛdhrikā</s>, <s>Śuci</s>, and <s>Sugrīvā</s>; from them arose crows and the rest.

children.text: aśvāścoṣṭrāś ca tāmrāyā aruṇo garuḍas tathā ||
children.translated_text: Horses and camels came from <s>Tāmrā</s>, and <s>Aruṇa</s> and <s>Garuḍa</s> as well.

children.text: vinatāyāḥ sahasraṃ tu sarpāś ca surasābhavāḥ
children.translated_text: From <s>Vinatā</s> came a thousand; and the serpents were born from <s>Surasā</s>.
The sons of <s>Kadrū</s> were a thousand, including <s>Śeṣa</s>, <s>Vāsuki</s>, and <s>Takṣaka</s>.
The fanged creatures were born of <s>Krodhavaśā</s>; the birds arose from <s>Dharā</s>, in the waters.
From <s>Surabhī</s> came cows, buffaloes, and the rest; from <s>Irā</s> arose grasses and the like.
From <s>Svasā</s> came yakṣas and rākṣasas, and from <s>Muni</s> came the <s>Aśvarasas</s>.

children.text: ariṣṭāyāṃ tu gandharvāḥ kaśyapāddhi sthiraṃ caraṃ ||
children.translated_text: From <s>Ariṣṭā</s> came the gandharvas, from <s>Kaśyapa</s>; moving and unmoving beings are thus established.

children.text: eṣāṃ putrādayo 'saṅkhyā devair vai dānavā jitāḥ
children.translated_text: Their sons and descendants are countless; the dānavas were defeated by the gods.
<s>Diti</s>, whose sons had been destroyed, propitiated <s>Kaśyapa</s>.
Desiring a son who would strike down <s>Indra</s>, she obtained one from <s>Kaśyapa</s>.

children.text: pādāprakṣālanāt suptā tasyā garbhaṃ jaghāna ha ||
children.translated_text: When she slept without washing her feet, he indeed struck her embryo.
Finding a breach, <s>Indra</s> cut it apart; those gods became the <s>Maruts</s>.
They were forty-nine helpers of <s>Śakra</s>, blazing with splendor.
<s>Hari</s>, who is <s>Brahmā</s>, consecrated <s>Pṛthu</s> as king over all this
and gave kingdoms in due order; <s>Hari</s> is the lord of the others.

children.text: dvijauṣadhīnāṃ candraś ca apāṃ tu varuṇo nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: The moon is king of brahmins and herbs, and <s>Varuṇa</s>, O king, is lord of the waters.
<s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> is king of kings, and the lord of the suns is <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: vasūnāṃ pāvako rājā marutāṃ vāsavaḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Pāvaka</s> is king of the Vasus, and <s>Vāsava</s> is lord of the Maruts.
<s>Dakṣa</s> is king of the Prajāpatis, and <s>Prahlāda</s> is lord of the dānavas.

children.text: pitṝṇāṃ ca yamo rājā bhūtādīnāṃ haraḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s> is king of the ancestors, and <s>Hara</s> is lord of beings and the rest.

children.text: himavāṃś caiva śailānāṃ nadīnāṃ sāgaraḥ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Himavat</s> is lord of mountains, and the ocean is lord of rivers.
Among the gandharvas the lord is <s>Citraratha</s>, and among the nāgas it is <s>Vāsuki</s>.
<s>Takṣaka</s> is king of serpents, and <s>Garuḍa</s> is king of birds.
<s>Airāvata</s> is lord of elephants, and the bull is lord of cattle.
Among wild animals the tiger is lord, and the plakṣa is lord of forest trees.
<s>Uccaiḥśravas</s> is lord of horses, and <s>Sudhanvan</s> is guardian of the east.
In the south <s>Śaṅkhapada</s> is guardian, and <s>Ketumān</s> is guardian in the waters.
<s>Hiraṇyaromaka</s> is guardian in the northern quarter; this secondary creation has been declared.

children.text: ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye pratisargavarṇanaṃ nāma ūnaviṃśatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the primordial great Purāṇa, the Āgneya, the nineteenth chapter, called 'The Description of Secondary Creation.'
<s>Agni</s> said:

children.text: prathamo mahataḥ sargo vijñeyo brahmaṇastu saḥ
children.translated_text: The first creation should be known as the creation of the great principle; it belongs to <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: tanmātrāṇāṃ dvitīyastu bhūtasargo hi sa smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The second is the creation of the subtle elements; it is remembered as the creation of the elements.
The third is the vaikārika creation, remembered as the creation of the senses.
This is the prākṛta (primary) creation, produced with prior intelligence.

children.text: mukhyaḥ sargaś caturthastu mukhyā vai sthāvarāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: The fourth creation is the chief one; the chief beings are remembered as the immobile ones.
That which is called the downward-streaming creation is then remembered as the creation of animals.
The sixth, of those whose stream is upward, is remembered as the creation of gods.

children.text: tato 'rvāksrotasāṃ sargaḥ saptamaḥ sa tu mānuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the creation of those whose stream is downward is the seventh, the human creation.
The eighth is the creation of favor, which is both sāttvika and tāmasa.

children.text: pañcaite vaikṛtāḥ sargāḥ prākṛtāś ca trayaḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These five are the vaikṛta creations, and three are remembered as prākṛta.

children.text: prākṛto vaikṛtaś caiva kaumāro navamas tathā
children.translated_text: There is the prākṛta and the vaikṛta, and likewise the kaumāra as the ninth.
Thus from <s>Brahmā</s> there are nine creations, the root causes of the world.
The daughters of <s>Dakṣa</s>, beginning with <s>Khyāti</s>, married <s>Bhṛgu</s> and the others.
Creation is spoken of by people as threefold: perpetual and occasional.
The prākṛta creation is daily, after the intermediate dissolution.
Where it arises day by day, that is accepted as perpetual creation.
<s>Khyāti</s> bore the two gods <s>Dhātṛ</s> and <s>Vidhātṛ</s> to <s>Bhṛgu</s>,

children.text: śriyaṃ ca patnī viṣṇoryā stutā śakreṇa vṛddhaye ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Śrī</s>, the wife of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who was praised by <s>Śakra</s> for prosperity.

children.text: dhātur vidhātur dvau putrau kramāt prāṇo mṛkaṇḍukaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Dhātṛ</s> and <s>Vidhātṛ</s> had two sons in order, <s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Mṛkaṇḍuka</s>.
From <s>Mṛkaṇḍu</s> was born <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, and from him <s>Vedaśiras</s>.
<s>Paurṇamāsa</s>, son of <s>Marīci</s>, was born from <s>Sambhūti</s>.
The sons of <s>Aṅgiras</s> by <s>Smṛti</s> were <s>Sinīvālī</s> and also <s>Kuhū</s>,
<s>Rākā</s> and <s>Anumati</s>; and <s>Anasūyā</s> bore to <s>Atri</s>

children.text: somaṃ durvāsasaṃ putraṃ dattātreyaṃ ca yoginam ||
children.translated_text: the sons <s>Soma</s>, <s>Durvāsas</s>, and the yogin <s>Dattātreya</s>.
In <s>Prīti</s>, the wife of <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Dattoli</s> was born as his son.
From <s>Kṣamā</s> by <s>Pulaha</s> were born <s>Sahiṣṇu</s> and the <s>Karmapādikas</s>.
And from <s>Saṃnati</s> by <s>Kratu</s> arose the <s>Bālakhilyas</s> of great might,
sixty thousand in number, each the size of a thumb-joint.
From <s>Ūrjā</s> by <s>Vaśiṣṭha</s> came <s>Rāja</s>, <s>Gātra</s>, and <s>Ūrdhvabāhu</s>,
<s>Savana</s>, <s>Anagha</s>, <s>Śukra</s>, and <s>Sutapas</s>, the seven sages.
<s>Pāvaka</s>, <s>Pavamāna</s>, and <s>Śuci</s> were born; they were the fire-born sons of <s>Svāhā</s>.
The <s>Agnisvāttas</s> and <s>Barhiṣads</s>, without fire and with fire, were born.

children.text: pitṛbhyaś ca svadhāyāṃ ca menā vaidhāriṇī sute
children.translated_text: And from <s>Svadhā</s> by the Pitṛs came two daughters, <s>Menā</s> and <s>Vaidhāriṇī</s>.
<s>Hiṃsā</s> was the wife of <s>Adharma</s>, and from those two was born <s>Anṛta</s>.
And from them came a daughter, <s>Nikṛti</s>, and also <s>Bhaya</s> and <s>Naraka</s>.

children.text: māyā ca vedanā caiva mithunaṃ tvidametayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Māyā</s> and <s>Vedanā</s> also formed a pair born from these two.
From them, then, <s>Māyā</s> bore <s>Mṛtyu</s>, the taker-away of beings.

children.text: vedanā ca sutaṃ cāpi duḥkhaṃ jajñe 'tha rauravāt ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Vedanā</s> bore a son, <s>Duḥkha</s>, from <s>Raurava</s>.
From <s>Mṛtyu</s> were born disease, old age, sorrow, thirst, and anger.
From <s>Brahmā</s> was born one who cried; because of his crying he was named <s>Rudra</s>.
O brahmin, <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Śarva</s>, then <s>Īśāna</s>, and likewise <s>Paśupati</s>
The grandfather addressed <s>Bhīma</s>, the fierce great god.

children.text: dakṣakopācca tadbhāryā dehaṃ tatyāja sā satī
children.translated_text: Because of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s anger, his wife <s>Satī</s> abandoned her body.
Having become the daughter of <s>Himavat</s>, she again became the wife of <s>Śambhu</s>.
The forms of worship, beginning with bathing, taught by <s>Nārada</s> and the others to the sages,
beginning with the self-born one, when performed, grant enjoyment and liberation from <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the rest.

children.text: ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye jagatsargavarṇanaṃ nāma viṃśatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the primordial great Purāṇa, the Āgneya, the twentieth chapter, called 'The Description of the Creation of the World.'
<s>Nārada</s> said:
I shall teach the general worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the others, and the mantras that always give gifts.
One should worship, saying, 'Homage to <s>Acyuta</s> together with his entire retinue.'

children.text: dhātre vidhātre gaṅgāyai yamunāyai nidhī tathā
children.translated_text: One should worship <s>Dhātṛ</s>, <s>Vidhātṛ</s>, <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Yamunā</s>, and the two treasures,
the prosperity of the doorway, the new vastu, <s>Śakti</s>, <s>Kūrma</s>, and <s>Ananta</s>.
One should worship the earth, dharma, knowledge, detachment, and sovereignty,
and adharma and the others, the stalk, stem, petals, filaments, and pericarp of the lotus.
One should worship the spheres beginning with the Ṛgveda, beginning with the Kṛta age, and beginning with sattva and the sun.

children.text: vimalotkarṣiṇī jñānā kriyā yogā ca tā yajet ||
children.translated_text: One should worship <s>Vimalā</s>, <s>Utkarṣiṇī</s>, <s>Jñānā</s>, <s>Kriyā</s>, and <s>Yogā</s>.
One should worship <s>Prahvī</s>, <s>Satyā</s>, and the seat-form embodying the grace of <s>Īśāna</s>.
One should worship <s>Durgā</s>, speech, the courtyard, the field, and <s>Vāsudeva</s> and the others.
One should worship the heart, head, spear, armor, eye, and then the missile,

children.text: śaṅkhaṃ cakraṃ gadāṃ padmaṃ śrīvatsaṃ kaustubhaṃ yajet ||
children.translated_text: the conch, discus, mace, lotus, <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, and <s>Kaustubha</s>.
One should honor the forest garland, <s>Śrī</s>, nourishment, <s>Garuḍa</s>, and the guru.

children.text: indramagniṃ yamaṃ rakṣo jalaṃ vāyuṃ dhaneśvaram ||
children.translated_text: One should worship <s>Indra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Yama</s>, the demon, water, wind, and the lord of wealth.
One should worship <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, the unborn one, the missile, the vehicle, and <s>Kumuda</s> and the others.
By worship beginning with <s>Viṣvaksena</s> at the maṇḍala and so on, accomplishment comes about.
Now the general worship of <s>Śiva</s>: first one should honor <s>Nandin</s>.
One should worship <s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Yamunā</s>, and the gaṇas and the rest.

children.text: giraṃ śriyaṃ guruṃ vāstuṃ śakyādīn dharmakādikam
children.translated_text: One should worship speech, <s>Śrī</s>, the guru, vastu, <s>Śakyā</s> and the others, and dharma and the rest.

children.text: vāmā jyeṣṭhā tathā raudrī kālī kalavikāriṇī ||
children.translated_text: In order, one should worship <s>Vāmā</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Raudrī</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, and <s>Kalavikāriṇī</s>,
and also <s>Balavikariṇī</s> and <s>Balapramathinī</s>.
One should worship <s>Sarvabhūtadamanī</s>, <s>Madanonmādinī</s>, and the seat of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: hāṃ huṃ hāṃ śivamūrtaye sāṅgavaktraṃ śivaṃ yajet
children.translated_text: With 'hāṃ huṃ hāṃ, to the form of <s>Śiva</s>,' one should worship <s>Śiva</s> with his limbs and faces.
With 'hauṃ, to <s>Śiva</s>; hām' and the like, one should worship the faces beginning with <s>Īśāna</s>.

children.text: hrīṃ gaurīṃ gaṃ gaṇaḥ śakramukhāś caṇḍīhṛtādikāḥ
children.translated_text: With 'hrīṃ' one should worship <s>Gaurī</s>; with 'gaṃ,' the gaṇa; and the faces beginning with <s>Śakra</s>, with <s>Caṇḍī</s>, the heart, and the rest.

children.text: kramātsūryārcane mantrā daṇḍī pūjyaś ca piṅgalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In order, in the worship of the sun, the mantras are as follows: <s>Daṇḍin</s> and <s>Piṅgala</s> are to be worshiped.
One should worship <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s>, <s>Aruṇa</s>, <s>Prabhūta</s>, and <s>Vimala</s>.
One should worship <s>Sārādhya</s>, supreme bliss, and <s>Skanda</s> and the others in the middle.

children.text: dīptā sūkṣmā jayā bhadrā vibhūtirvimalā tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Dīptā</s>, <s>Sūkṣmā</s>, <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Bhadrā</s>, <s>Vibhūti</s>, and <s>Vimalā</s>,
as well as <s>Amoghā</s>, <s>Vidyutā</s>, and <s>Sarvatomukhī</s>, are then to be worshiped.

children.text: arkāsanaṃ hi haṃ khaṃ kha solkāyeti ca mūrtikām
children.translated_text: The seat of <s>Arka</s> is to be worshiped, and the image with the formula 'hi haṃ khaṃ kha solkāya.'

children.text: hrāṃ hrīṃ sa sūryāya nama āṃ namo hṛdāya ca ||
children.translated_text: The mantra is 'hrāṃ hrīṃ sa, homage to <s>Sūrya</s>; āṃ, homage to the heart.'
Likewise for the head of <s>Arka</s>, and for those belonging to fire, <s>Īśa</s>, demons, and wind.

children.text: bhūrbhuvaḥ svare jvālini śikhā huṃ kavacaṃ smṛtaṃ ||
children.translated_text: 'Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, O blazing one'; the topknot is remembered with 'huṃ' as armor.

children.text: bhāṃ netraṃ vas tathārkāstraṃ rājñī śaktiś ca niṣkubhā
children.translated_text: 'Bhāṃ' is for the eye, and 'vas' likewise is the solar missile; <s>Rājñī</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, and <s>Niṣkubhā</s> are worshiped.

children.text: somo 'ṅgārakotha budho jīvaḥ śukraḥ śaniḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: Then in order come <s>Soma</s>, <s>Aṅgāraka</s>, <s>Budha</s>, <s>Jīva</s>, <s>Śukra</s>, and <s>Śani</s>.
<s>Rāhu</s>, <s>Ketu</s>, <s>Tejas</s>, and <s>Caṇḍa</s> are worshiped; now, in brief, the worship is given.
The seat, the image, the root mantra, the heart and the others, and the attendants are worshiped.

children.text: viṣṇvāsanaṃ viṣṇurmūrteroṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ śrīdharo hariḥ
children.translated_text: The seat of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s> as the image are worshiped with 'oṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ, <s>Śrīdhara</s>, <s>Hari</s>.'
This mantra, 'hrīṃ, all-formed one,' is the deluder of the three worlds.

children.text: hrīṃ hṛṣīkeśaḥ klīṃ viṣṇuḥ svarair dīrghair hṛdādikaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Hrīṃ, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>; klīṃ, <s>Viṣṇu</s>': with the long vowels one performs the heart and the other rites.
With all of them, the fifth-case worship gives victory and the like in battle and other undertakings.
One should worship in order the discus, mace, conch, pestle, sword, and Śārṅga bow,
the noose and goad, <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, <s>Kaustubha</s>, and the forest garland.
With 'śrīṃ,' one worships <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Mahālakṣmī</s>, <s>Tārkṣya</s>, the guru, <s>Indra</s>, and the others.
For <s>Sarasvatī</s>, her seat and image are worshiped with 'auṃ hrīṃ dadhī, <s>Sarasvatī</s>.'

children.text: hṛdādyā lakṣmīrmedhā ca kalātuṣṭiś ca puṣṭikā
children.translated_text: Her heart and other limbs are worshiped, along with <s>Lakṣmī</s>, intelligence, art, satisfaction, and nourishment.

children.text: gaurī prabhāmatī durgā gaṇo guruś ca kṣetrapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Prabhāmatī</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, the gaṇa, the guru, and the guardian of the field are also worshiped.

children.text: tathā gaṃ gaṇapataye ca hrīṃ gauryai ca śrīṃ śriyai
children.translated_text: Likewise the mantras are 'gaṃ, to <s>Gaṇapati</s>,' 'hrīṃ, to <s>Gaurī</s>,' and 'śrīṃ, to <s>Śrī</s>.'

children.text: hrīṃ tvaritāyai hrīṃ sau tripurā caturthyantanamontakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Hrīṃ, to <s>Tvaritā</s>,' and 'hrīṃ sau, <s>Tripurā</s>': the names ending in the fourth case end with 'namaḥ.'
The mantras may begin with the praṇava, and the first syllable of the name may be joined with the bindu.
Or they may be joined with 'oṃ'; by worship and recitation with all mantras, they are remembered.
By oblations with sesame, ghee, and the like, they grant dharma, desire, wealth, and liberation.
Whoever recites the worship mantras, having enjoyed pleasures, goes to heaven.

children.text: ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye vāsudevādipūjākathanaṃ nāma ekaviṃśatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the primordial great Purāṇa, the Āgneya, the twenty-first chapter, called 'The Explanation of the Worship of <s>Vāsudeva</s> and the Others.'
<s>Agni</s> said:
The dhanurveda, having four feet, is taught in the Veda as fivefold, O twice-born one,
with reference to chariot-warriors, elephant-warriors, cavalry, infantry, and other fighters.
That which is released, that which is released by the hand, that which is released while retained,

children.text: amuktaṃ bāhuyuddhaṃ ca pañcadhā tat prakīrtitaṃ ||
children.translated_text: that which is not released, and arm-fighting: it is declared to be fivefold.
There it is said to be twofold according to the possession of śastra and astra, weapons and missiles.
Again it is called twofold according to the distinction between straight fighting and deceptive fighting.
That which is released by machines such as throwing engines and bows is called machine-released.
That which includes stones, javelins, and similar implements is called hand-released.
That which can also be held after being cast should be known as released-and-retained.
Swords and the like are unreleased, and niyuddha is combat without weapons.
One who wishes to fight and has conquered fatigue should make suitable protections.
The best battles are those fought with bows, and those with spears are middling.
Those fought with swords are inferior, and those fought with the arms are lower still.
In the science of the bow, a Brahmin is declared to be the teacher for the two varṇas.
A Śūdra's right to fight is through training that brings about his own striking skill.

children.text: deśasthaiḥ śaṅkarai rājñaḥ kāryā yuddhe sahāyatā ||
children.translated_text: Those established in the country, the mixed troops, should give assistance to the king in battle.
If the big toes, ankles, hands, and feet are close-set and joined together,
this posture, according to its marks, is seen as the <s>samapada</s> (even-footed) stance.
When both feet stand on the outer toes and both knees and thighs are firm,
this stance, with an interval of three spans, is called <s>vaiśākha</s>.
Where the knees appear equal in the shape of a row of geese,
and are separated by four spans, that is remembered as the <s>maṇḍala</s> stance.
That which has the form of a plough, with the right knee and thigh held firm,
and is five spans in breadth, is proclaimed to be <s>ālīḍha</s>.
This same stance reversed is remembered as <s>pratyālīḍha</s>.
The left should be turned crosswise, while the right should be straight.
The ankles, together with the heel-grips, are set five finger-breadths apart.
This stance is produced, extending twelve finger-breadths.
The left knee should be straight and the right well extended,

children.text: athavā dakṣiṇaṃ jānu kubjaṃ bhavati niścalaṃ ||
children.translated_text: or else the right knee is bent and motionless.
This foot, together with the knee, should be stretched out like a staff.
Thus the <s>vikaṭa</s> stance is taught, extending across an interval of two hands.
The knees should be doubled, and both feet should be turned upward.
By this application of the rule, the <s>sampuṭa</s> stance is proclaimed.
The feet are somewhat turned about, steady and extended like equal staffs.
As prescribed, this very stance is seen to extend sixteen finger-breadths.
Here, O Brahmin, one should first make obeisance in the <s>svastika</s> posture.

children.text: kārmukaṃ gṛhya vāmena bāṇaṃ dakṣiṇakena tu ||
children.translated_text: One should take the bow with the left hand, and the arrow with the right.

children.text: vaiśākhe yadi vā jāte sthitau vāpyathavāyatau
children.translated_text: Whether standing in the <s>vaiśākha</s> posture, in the produced stance, or in the extended stance,

children.text: guṇāntaṃ tu tataḥ kṛtvā kārmuke priyakārmukaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, having brought it to the end of the string on the bow, the lover of bows should proceed.

children.text: adhaḥkaṭiṃ tu dhanuṣaḥ phaladeśaṃ tu patriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: He should place the lower waist of the bow and the feathered part of the arrow

children.text: dharaṇyāṃ sthāpayitvā tu tolayitvā tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: on the ground, and then weigh and balance them in the same way.
With the two arms bent here, and with the forearms, O one of good vows,

children.text: yasya bāṇaṃ dhanuḥ śreṣṭhaṃ puṅgadeśe ca patriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for one whose arrow and bow are excellent, and at the feathered end of the arrow,
the placing of the bow should have an interval of twelve finger-breadths.

children.text: jyayā viśiṣṭaḥ kartavyo nātihīno na cādhikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It should be made distinct by the bowstring, neither too deficient nor excessive.
Having set the bow at the navel and the cluster of arrows at the hip,
he should raise the lifted hand between the eye and the ear.
The arrow should be grasped with the forward fist at the right nipple.

children.text: haraṇaṃ tu tataḥ kṛtvā śīghraṃ pūrvaṃ prasārayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, having performed the drawing, he should quickly extend the forward part.

children.text: nābhyantarā naiva bāhyā nordhvakā nādharā tathā
children.translated_text: It should be neither inward nor outward, neither upward nor downward,

children.text: na ca kubjā na cottānā na calā nātiveṣṭitā ||
children.translated_text: neither bent nor turned upward, neither unsteady nor excessively twisted.
It should be even, endowed with firmness, and positioned like the forward staff.
Then, having covered the target with this forward fist,
the shooter, raised at the chest, should stand bent in a triangular posture.
His shoulders should be lowered, his neck motionless, and his head bent like a peacock's.
The forehead, nose, mouth, and shoulders should be made even like those of a horse.
The interval between the chin and the shoulder should be known as three finger-breadths.

children.text: prathamaṃ tryaṅgulaṃ jñeyaṃ dvitīye dvyaṅgulaṃ smṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: In the first case it should be known as three finger-breadths; in the second, two finger-breadths are remembered.
In the third, the distance between chin and shoulder is taught as one finger-breadth.
Having taken the arrow by the feathered end with the forefinger and thumb,
and then grasping it also with the ring finger and likewise with the middle finger,
he should draw it forcefully until the arrow is fully drawn.
Having undertaken it in this manner, the feathered shaft should be released according to rule.
A well-disciplined man should pierce with the arrow the target struck by his sight and fist.

children.text: muktvā tu paścimaṃ hastaṃ kṣipedvegena pṛṣṭhataḥ ||
children.translated_text: After releasing, he should fling the rear hand swiftly backward.
They call this the cutting-off; indeed it is to be understood by you, O Brahmin.
The archer, after drawing the bow, should set the elbow below it.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ vimuktake kārye lakṣaśliṣṭaṃ tu madhyamaṃ
children.translated_text: When the release is to be made upward, the middle should be made close to the target.
By those skilled in the bow-science, the best bow is to be understood as the fully drawn one.
The largest arrow should be known as measuring twelve fists.
The smaller one is eleven, and the smallest is ten fists.

children.text: caturhastaṃ dhanuḥ śreṣṭhaṃ trayaḥ sārdhaṃ tu madhyamaṃ
children.translated_text: For a foot-soldier, the best bow is four hands long; the middle one is three and a half.
The smallest is said to be three hands, always for the foot-soldier.

children.text: aśve rathe gaje śreṣṭhe tadeva parikīrtitaṃ ||
children.translated_text: On a horse, in a chariot, and on an excellent elephant, the same is declared.

children.text: ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe dhanurvedo nāma aṣṭacatvāriṃśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the great <s>Āgneya Purāṇa</s>, the chapter named 'Dhanurveda,' the two-hundred-and-forty-eighth chapter.
<s>Agni</s> said:

children.text: pūrṇāyataṃ dvijaḥ kṛtvā tato māṃsair gadāyudhān
children.translated_text: After the Brahmin has made the full extension, then, with pieces of flesh, those armed with clubs...
Having made the bow well cleansed, he should have it set up on the sacrificial ground.
Then, having taken up the arrow, armored and well composed,
he should quickly approach and fasten the firm right armpit-strap.
That arrow, though not aimed at a target, should be well positioned there itself.
Then he should draw the arrow from the quiver with his right hand.

children.text: tenaiva sahitaṃ madhye śaraṃ saṃgṛhya dhārayet
children.translated_text: Together with that, he should grasp and hold the arrow in the middle.
With the left hand he should take up the armpit-strap and then the bow from it.
Becoming free from dejection in mind, he should set the feathered end on the string.
Having pressed it firmly with the lion-ear grip, and also evenly with the feathered end,
he should hold the left-side fruit, set beside the left ear.

children.text: varṇān madhyamayā tatra vāmāṅgulyā ca dhārayet ||
children.translated_text: There he should hold the syllables with the middle finger and with the left finger.

children.text: mano lakṣyagataṃ kṛtvā muṣṭinā ca vidhānavit
children.translated_text: The man who knows the rule, having fixed his mind on the target, with his fist

children.text: dakṣiṇe gātrabhāge tu kṛtvā varṇaṃ vimokṣayet ||
children.translated_text: should set the syllable on the right side of the body and release it.
He should place the staff, positioned at the opening of the forehead, upon the target.
Having drawn it, he should strike there the candraka measuring sixteen finger-breadths.
Then, after releasing the arrow, at that time, by that firebrand training,
he should check it with the middle finger, again and again.
He should shoot an eye-target from the quiver, and also a square one on the right.
Standing at the beginning, he should practice hitting the mark set in the square.

children.text: tasmādanantaraṃ tīkṣṇaṃ parāvṛttaṃ gataṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: After that, he should practice what is sharp, turned back, and moving,
and then the low and high shots, quickly.
Then, in these target positions, from the casing of the bow's strength,
he should menace even difficult targets with hundreds of varied hand-insertions.

children.text: tasmin vedhyagate vipra dve vedhye dṛḍhasaṃjñake
children.translated_text: When the target has been reached, O brahmin, two targets are called firm targets;

children.text: dve vedhye duṣkare vedhye dve tathā citraduṣkare ||
children.translated_text: two targets are difficult targets, and two likewise are variegated difficult targets.

children.text: na tu nimnaṃ ca tīkṣṇaṃ ca dṛḍhavedhye prakīrtite
children.translated_text: But the low and the sharp are not declared to be firm targets.

children.text: nimnaṃ duṣkaramuddiṣṭaṃ vedhyam ūrdhvagataṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: The low one is called difficult, and so is the target that goes upward.
Those in the middle of the course to the head are called variegated difficult targets.
Having thus made the group of targets, with the right and with the other hand,
the hero, the man who has conquered the target, should first mount upward.

children.text: eṣa eva vidhiḥ proktastatra dṛṣṭaḥ prayoktṛbhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: This very procedure has been taught there and is seen among practitioners.
Its greater circling is said to be from that target.
There he should set a firm target placed leaf upon leaf.

children.text: bhrāntaṃ pracalitaṃ caiva sthiraṃ yacca bhavediti
children.translated_text: Whether it is whirling, moving, or steady,
he should strike it from every side, split it, cut it, and pierce it as well.
Knowing the procedure for the application of action, he should practice the rule in this way.
The student of discipline should conquer restraint with mind, eye, and sight.
Thus in the great <s>Āgneya Purāṇa</s>, the chapter called <s>Dhanurveda</s>, the two-hundred forty-ninth chapter.
<s>Agni</s> said:
Having mastered his hand, mastered his mind, mastered his gaze, and become an accomplisher of targets,
after attaining fixed success, he should then mount a vehicle.

children.text: daśahasto bhavet pāśo vṛttaḥ karamukhas tathā
children.translated_text: The noose should be ten cubits long, round, and with a hand-sized mouth,
made from cords of cotton, muñja grass, hemp, sinew, arka fiber, or hide,
or from other very strong materials, well made and wrapped around.

children.text: tathā triṃśatsamaṃ pāśaṃ budhaḥ kuryāt suvartitam ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, the wise man should make a noose equal to thirty cubits, well twisted.

children.text: kartavyaṃ śikṣakaistasya sthānaṃ kakṣāsu vai tadā
children.translated_text: Its station should then be prepared by instructors in the training grounds.
Taking it with the left hand, he should then raise it with the right.
Having made the shape of a ring and whirled it above his head,
he should quickly cast it, swiftly, at a man covered in leather.

children.text: valgite ca plute caiva tathā pravrajiteṣu ca
children.translated_text: Against those who are prancing, leaping, and likewise moving away,
having observed the proper method of timing, he should use it when well trained.

children.text: vijitvā tu yathānyāyaṃ tato bandhaṃ samācaret
children.translated_text: After conquering according to rule, he should then perform the binding.
Then, having fastened the sword at the waist, hanging down on the left side,
he should grasp it firmly with the left and draw it out with the right.
There should be iron rods six finger-breadths in circumference and seven cubits high,

children.text: ayomayyaḥ śalākāś ca varmāṇi vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: and various armors as well,
at half a cubit, level, and also going obliquely and upward.
He should arrange them according to the rule; now hear from me about the striking limb.
Having set up a new, firm figure whose body is bound with quiver-leather,
taking in the hand a club, nine right-finger-breadths long,
he should raise it and strike; by that the firm destruction of the pupil's weakness is made.
Then with both hands he should bring about its fall.

children.text: akleśena tataḥ kurvan badhe siddhiḥ prakīrtitā ||
children.translated_text: When he does this without strain, success in striking is declared.
The tiring of mounts for the sake of exercise was formerly taught to you.
Thus in the great <s>Āgneya Purāṇa</s>, the chapter called <s>Dhanurveda</s>, the two-hundred fiftieth chapter.
<s>Agni</s> said:
The whirled, the over-whirled, the cast, the leapt, the counter-leapt, the advanced,
the pounce, the upward-facing, the hawk's fall, and the confused,
the shaken up, the shaken down, the leftward and the rightward,
the unseen and the bursting, the terrible-handed and the great companion of <s>Indra</s>,
the frightful falls and the terrifying and fearsome ones,
the whole, half, third-part, quarter, half-quarter, and lotus-born forms,
the pratyālīḍha stance, the ālīḍha stance, the boar, and the rolling movement,
these thirty-two are to be known in the method of sword and shield in battle.
The turned back, the turned away, the seized, called light,
the cast upward, the cast downward, the held and the divided,
the hawk's fall, the elephant's fall, and the seized-and-seizer like a crocodile:
thus, O men, eleven kinds are to be known in the method of the noose.
Straight and extended, broad, and also whirled crosswise:
five actions are prescribed by the great-souled ones when the noose is separated.

children.text: chedanaṃ bhedanaṃ pāto bhramaṇaṃ śayanaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Cutting, splitting, falling, whirling, and lying down,
slicing and cutting too: this is the discus-action.
The striking, driving, splitting, frightening, and shaking movements,
know these as spear-actions, with the sixth called the blow.
O best of twice-born men, the eye-strike, the arm-strike, and the side-strike,
and a fall with a straight-winged arrow are proclaimed as actions of the tomara.
O brahmin, the struck posture, the cow-urine pattern, the abundant one, the lotus-seat,
then the body raised upward, bent, and also to the left and right,
the turning around, the turning back, the foot-raised, and the leaping,
the goose-crushing and the grinding: these are proclaimed as actions of the mace.
The terrible one, the downward blow, and the tenfold leaping,
the thrown-hand, the standing, and the empty posture should be specified for the paraśu.

children.text: tāḍanaṃ chedanaṃ vipra tathā cūrṇanameva ca
children.translated_text: Striking, cutting, O brahmin, and likewise crushing
are the actions of the mudgara, and also leaping and striking.
The wearied, the rested, the cow-release, and the very hard-to-withstand
are actions of the bhindipāla; they are also those of the club.
The final, the middle, the turned-back, and the one ending in command, O best of twice-born men:
these are the actions of the vajra, and they are also those of the paṭṭiśa.
Seizing, cutting, striking, lifting by strength, and the extended action
are taught as the actions of the sword, along with felling and bursting.
Frightening, guarding, striking, lifting by strength, and the extended action
are taught as the work of a throwing weapon; this also is the work of a machine.
Abandoning, biting, and the boar-upheaval,
hand-to-hand, reversed-hand, garlanded, one-hand, and hand-to-hand again,
two-handed, arm-noose, waist-twisted, and raised up,
strikes to the chest and forehead, and also shaking with the arms,
hand-raised, aerial, foot-blow, and counter-foot,
joining the limbs, the pacified move, and the reversal of limbs,
the upward blow, the strike, the cow-urine pattern, to the left and right,
the crossing-over, the staff, the confused karavīra-opening,
the transverse binding, the apāmārga, the terrible-rush, and the sudarśana,
the lion's stride, the elephant's stride, and also the donkey's stride:
one should know these as actions of the mace; next come the actions of wrestling.
Pulling and pushing, and the root of the arms,
turning the neck around, and the very terrible breaking of the back,
overthrowing and reversing, the beast-killing, and the goat-sheep move,
the foot-blow, the slap, and the waist-twisting,
embracing the limbs, going to the shoulder, and the earth-feint,
the chest-and-forehead strike and likewise the clear execution,
the raised-up, the shaken-off, and the one moving on a sideways path,
the elephant-shoulder, the throwing down, and the one facing away,
the divine path, the downward path, and the confused going off the path,
the staff-blow, the throwing down, and the splitting of the earth,
the knee-binding and the arm-binding, very terrible,
the back-turned, the water-filled, the bright, and the arm-encircled:
in battle one should be equipped with armored men, armed with weapons, on elephants and the like.
Two should carry excellent goads; one should be stationed at the neck and another

children.text: skandhau dvau ca dhānuṣkau dvau ca khaḍgadharau gaje ||
children.translated_text: at the shoulders; on an elephant there should be two archers and two sword-bearers.

children.text: rathe raṇe gaje caiva turagāṇāṃ trayaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: In war, on a chariot and on an elephant, there should be three horsemen;
three archers are prescribed also for the protection of the horse.
For the protection of an archer, one should appoint a shield-bearer.
Having worshiped the weapon with its own mantras, the śāstra is the deluder of the three worlds.

children.text: yo yuddhe yāti ca jayedarīn sampālayedbhuvaṃ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever goes to battle in this way conquers his enemies and protects the earth.
Thus, in the great <s>Agnipurāṇa</s>, the two-hundred-fifty-first chapter, called Dhanurveda.
